query_prefix:
Instruct: Given a query, retrieve relevant Swiss public-information concepts.
Query:

concepts.text:
Label: Authority issuing residence permits
Description: Which authority issues residence permits: the cantonal migration offices.
Aliases: which authority issues permits; kantonales Migrationsamt; cantonal migration office; Cantonal Migration Offices
Questions: Which office issues residence permits?; Bei welchem Amt beantrage ich eine Aufenthaltsbewilligung?
Published facts:
Residence permits are issued by the cantonal migration offices.

Label: AIG baseline for stays without work
Description: Federal baseline for stays without work: up to three months without a permit, longer stays need a permit applied for before entry (AIG Art. 10).
Aliases: stay without a permit; stay longer than three months without working; visit Switzerland without working; long stay without work; bewilligungsfreier Aufenthalt; länger als drei Monate bleiben; Aufenthalt ohne Erwerbstätigkeit; Bewilligungspflicht; drei Monaten keine Bewilligung; Visum
Questions: Do I need a permit to stay in Switzerland for a few months if I don't work?; Ab wann brauche ich eine Bewilligung, wenn ich mich ohne Arbeit in der Schweiz aufhalte?
Published facts:
AIG Article 10(1) states that a stay without gainful employment of up to three months does not require a residence permit; a shorter duration specified in the visa prevails.
For a planned longer stay without work, AIG Article 10(2) requires a permit application before entry to the authority at the intended place of residence, subject to Article 17(2).

Label: AIG employment permit procedure
Description: Federal rule that anyone working in Switzerland needs a permit regardless of duration, applied for by the employer (AIG Art. 11).
Aliases: Art. 11 AIG; permit required for gainful employment; employer applies for the permit; Bewilligung Erwerbstaetigkeit; Aufenthalt mit Erwerbstätigkeit; Erwerbstätigkeit; Bewilligungspflicht; Arbeitsort; Arbeitgeberin oder vom Arbeitgeber; selbständige Tätigkeit; Aufenthaltsdauer
Questions: Who applies for the work permit, the employee or the employer?; Do I need a work permit even for a temporary job?; Wer reicht das Bewilligungsgesuch ein, wenn ich eine Stelle antrete, ich oder der Arbeitgeber?
Published facts:
Under AIG Article 11(1), a foreign national intending to work in Switzerland needs a permit irrespective of the duration of stay and applies to the authority at the intended place of work.
AIG Article 11(2) includes activities normally performed for remuneration even when performed without pay; for employment, Article 11(3) assigns the permit application to the employer.

Label: Registration under AIG Article 12
Description: Federal duty to register with the authority at the place of residence before the permit-free stay ends or work starts, and when moving canton (AIG Art. 12).
Aliases: Einwohnermeldeamt; Meldeamt; ummelden; Anmeldung beim Einwohnermeldeamt; Anmeldepflicht Art. 12 AIG; register before starting work; registration when moving canton; Anmeldepflicht; Anmeldefristen; anmelden; Wohnort; andere Gemeinde; anderen Kanton; bewilligungsfreien Aufenthalts
Questions: Do I have to register when I move to another canton?; Muss ich mich bei der neuen Gemeinde anmelden, wenn ich umziehe?
Published facts:
Persons needing a short-stay, residence or settlement permit must register with the authority at their Swiss residence before the permit-free stay expires or before starting work.
AIG Article 12 requires registration with the authority at the new residence when moving to another municipality or canton; federal regulations determine the registration deadlines.

Label: Short-stay permit: AIG Article 32
Description: The short-stay permit L: fixed stay up to one year, purpose-bound, extendable to two years (AIG Art. 32).
Aliases: L permit; Kurzaufenthaltsbewilligung; short-stay permit up to one year; befristete Aufenthalte; Aufenthaltszweck; Stellenwechsel; angemessenen Unterbruch; zwei Jahren verlängert
Questions: What is an L permit?; Wie lange gilt eine Kurzaufenthaltsbewilligung, und kann man sie verlängern?
Published facts:
AIG Article 32 describes the short-stay permit as covering a fixed stay of up to one year, issued for a specified purpose and potentially subject to additional conditions.
Under AIG Article 32(3)-(4), a short-stay permit may be extended up to two years; changing jobs requires important reasons, and a new grant requires an appropriate interruption of the Swiss stay.

Label: Residence permit: AIG Article 33
Description: The residence permit B: stays longer than one year, purpose-bound, time-limited, renewable (AIG Art. 33).
Aliases: Aufenthaltserlaubnis; Aufenthaltstitel; B permit; Aufenthaltsbewilligung B; residence permit longer than one year; Aufenthaltsbewilligung; mehr als einem Jahr; befristet; verlängert; Widerrufsgründe; Gültigkeitsdauer; Integrationsvereinbarung; Integrationsbedarf
Questions: What is a B permit and how long is it valid?; Für welchen Zeitraum wird eine B-Bewilligung erteilt, und was gilt bei der Verlängerung?
Published facts:
AIG Article 33 defines the residence permit for stays longer than one year. It is purpose-bound, may carry additional conditions, and is time-limited.
A residence permit may be renewed if no revocation grounds under Article 62(1) exist. Integration is considered when setting its duration, and a special integration need can lead to an integration agreement.

Label: Settlement permit: AIG Article 34
Description: The settlement permit C: unlimited and unconditional, normally after ten years of residence (AIG Art. 34).
Aliases: permanent residence; permanent residency; PR; Niederlassungserlaubnis; unbefristete Aufenthaltserlaubnis; C permit; Niederlassungsbewilligung; settlement permit after ten years; unbefristet und ohne Bedingungen; mindestens zehn Jahre; letzten fünf Jahren ununterbrochen; Vorübergehende Aufenthalte; Aus- oder Weiterbildung; integriert; kürzeren Aufenthalt; Vorzeitige Erteilung; Integrationskriterien; Referenzniveau B1
Questions: When can I get a C permit?; Nach wie vielen Jahren mit B-Bewilligung bekomme ich den C-Ausweis?
Published facts:
The settlement permit is issued for an unlimited period and without conditions under AIG Article 34(1).
AIG Article 34(2) allows settlement after at least ten years with short-stay or residence permits, including the last five years continuously with a residence permit, provided the specified revocation grounds are absent and integration requirements are met. Paragraphs 3 and 4 provide shorter-stay routes, so ten years is not a universal waiting period.
For the continuous five-year period, temporary stays do not count. Education stays count when followed by two uninterrupted years with a residence permit for a durable stay, as specified by AIG Article 34(5).
VZAE Article 62: the early grant of the settlement permit under AIG Article 34(4) requires the integration criteria of AIG Article 58a(1) to be met, and the foreign national must show oral skills at least at reference level B1 and written skills at least at reference level A1 in the national language spoken at the place of residence. The degree of integration of family members older than twelve is taken into account when the application is examined.

Label: Settlement permit after five years: states with settlement agreements
Description: The settlement permit C after five instead of ten years: the states whose nationals SEM names, and why the free movement agreement itself does not grant it.
Aliases: C permit after five years; five-year settlement permit; settlement agreement countries; C-Bewilligung nach fünf Jahren; Niederlassungsbewilligung nach 5 Jahren; which nationalities get the C permit after five years; Niedergelassene; Niederlassungsvereinbarungen; Niederlassungsverträgen; Gegenrechtsüberlegungen; ordnungsgemässen und ununterbrochenen Aufenthalt von fünf Jahren; Freizügigkeitsabkommen
Questions: Which nationalities can get the C permit after five years instead of ten?; Ich bin Deutsche und lebe seit fünf Jahren in der Schweiz. Bekomme ich schon die Niederlassungsbewilligung?
Published facts:
SEM describes settled foreign nationals as persons who were granted the settlement permit after a stay of five or ten years in Switzerland. The right of residence is unlimited and may not be tied to conditions, and SEM sets the date from which the competent cantonal authorities may issue the settlement permit at the earliest.
For EU/EFTA nationals the grant of the settlement permit follows the provisions of the AIG and of the settlement agreements, because the free movement agreement with the EU contains no provisions on the settlement permit.
SEM names the nationals who receive the settlement permit after a lawful and uninterrupted stay of five years, on the basis of settlement treaties or of reciprocity and provided they meet the necessary conditions: Belgium, Denmark, Germany, Finland, France, Greece, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Austria, Portugal, Sweden and Spain, and of EFTA Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway. For nationals of the other EU member states no such agreements exist.

Label: Foreign-national permit types
Description: The permit cards ch.ch lists for EU/EFTA and third-country nationals, and which states are EU-27 and EFTA.
Aliases: permit types; what is permit G; what is permit Ci; Bewilligungsarten; Ausländerausweis Arten; Was ist der Ausweis G; which countries are EU or EFTA; cross-border commuter permit; F permit provisionally admitted foreigners; N permit asylum seekers; S permit temporary protection; Ausländerausweis; Freizügigkeitsabkommen; Drittstaaten; Kurzaufenthaltsbewilligung; Niederlassungsbewilligung; Grenzgängerbewilligung; Ausweis Ci; EFTA; Ausweis F; Ausweis N; Asylsuchende; Ausweis S; Schutzbedürftige
Questions: Which residence permit types exist in Switzerland?; Welche Ausweise gibt es für Ausländer?; Is Czechia an EU country for Swiss permits?
Published facts:
ch.ch lists the foreign-national permit cards by group. EU/EFTA nationals: L (short stay), B (residence), C (settlement), Ci (residence with gainful employment) and G (cross-border commuter), each marked EU/EFTA. Third-country nationals: B, C, Ci, G and L, plus F (provisionally admitted foreigners), N (asylum seekers) and S (temporary protection). The free-movement agreement makes entry and residence much easier for EU and EFTA citizens; rules for other countries are more restrictive. The page lists the 27 EU member states and the EFTA states Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland.

Label: EU/EFTA permit cards B, L, Ci and G
Description: What each EU/EFTA permit card stands for: the residence permit B, the short-stay permit L, the residence permit with gainful employment Ci and the cross-border commuter permit G (SEM).
Aliases: what is a B permit; what is an L permit; Ci permit meaning; G permit cross-border commuter; EU permit card types; Was bedeutet Ausweis B; Aufenthalter; Kurzaufenthalter; Grenzgänger; Gültigkeitsdauer von fünf Jahren; Online-Meldeverfahren; intergouvernementaler Organisationen; berufliche und geographische Mobilität
Questions: What is the difference between the B, L, Ci and G permits for EU citizens?; Was bedeutet der Ausweis L für EU-Bürgerinnen und wie lange gilt er?
Published facts:
SEM: residents (Ausweis B EU/EFTA) are foreign nationals who stay in Switzerland for a longer period for a particular purpose, with or without gainful employment. For nationals of EU/EFTA member states the residence permit is valid for five years and is granted on proof of an open-ended employment or one limited to at least 365 days. It is extended by five years when the conditions are still met, but the first extension can be limited to one year if the person has been involuntarily unemployed for more than twelve consecutive months.
SEM: short-stay residents (Ausweis L EU/EFTA) are foreign nationals who stay in Switzerland for a limited time, as a rule less than a year, for a particular purpose with or without gainful employment. EU/EFTA nationals are entitled to this permit when they can show an employment relationship in Switzerland of between three months and one year; employment of under three months in a calendar year needs no permit and is handled through the online notification procedure. The permit is valid for the duration of the employment.
SEM: the residence permit with gainful employment (Ausweis Ci EU/EFTA) is for family members of officials of intergovernmental organisations and for staff of foreign representations, namely their spouses and children up to the age of 25. Its validity is limited to the duration of the main holder's function.
SEM: cross-border commuters (Ausweis G EU/EFTA) are EU/EFTA nationals who live in an EU/EFTA state and work in Switzerland, as employees or self-employed, and who as a rule return to their foreign main residence daily or at least once a week. They enjoy occupational and geographical mobility: border zones no longer apply to them, so they may live anywhere in the EU/EFTA and work anywhere in Switzerland, the only condition being the weekly return to the foreign place of residence.

Label: Third-country permit cards Ci and G
Description: What the third-country permit cards Ci and G stand for, and the border-zone condition a third-country cross-border commuter must meet (SEM).
Aliases: Ci permit third country; G permit third country national; border zone commuter permit; Grenzgängerbewilligung Drittstaat; Grenzzone; Grenzgängerabkommen; dauerhaftes Anwesenheitsrecht; intergouvernementaler Organisationen; Kreditkartenformat
Questions: Can a third-country national get a cross-border commuter permit for Switzerland?; Welche Bedingungen gelten für den Ausweis G von Drittstaatsangehörigen?
Published facts:
SEM: the residence permit with gainful employment (Ausweis Ci) for third-country nationals is for family members of officials of intergovernmental organisations and for members of foreign representations, namely their spouses and children up to the age of 25. Its validity is limited to the duration of the main holder's function, and the card is not proof of the holder's identity.
SEM: third-country cross-border commuters (Ausweis G) live in the foreign border zone and work in the neighbouring Swiss border zone; the border zones are those laid down in the cross-border commuter agreements between Switzerland and its neighbouring states, and the commuter must return to the foreign place of residence at least once a week. A commuter permit can be granted to a third-country national only with a permanent right of presence in a neighbouring state of Switzerland and at least six months of residence in the border zone, and the labour-market rules apply. The first commuter permit is as a rule valid for one year, and the card is not proof of the holder's identity.
SEM: since November 2019 a credit-card format permit without a chip has been issued, rolled out canton by canton until it was fully introduced in February 2022. Nationals of EU and EFTA member states receive it, and so do some third-country nationals. The S card has been issued since February 2022 and the F and N cards followed in stages from December 2022.

Label: Travel documents for foreign nationals
Description: The travel documents and return visas SEM issues to foreign nationals, who can get which one, how to apply, and what they do not prove.
Aliases: travel document for refugees; passport for foreign national Switzerland; travel without national passport; Reiseausweis für Flüchtlinge; Pass für ausländische Person; Rückreisevisum; Reisedokumente; Rückreisevisa; Reiseausweise für Flüchtlinge; schriftenlose; fremdenpolizeiliche Ausweise; kantonalen Migrationsbehörde
Questions: I have no national passport. Can Switzerland issue me a travel document?; Wer stellt einen Reiseausweis für Flüchtlinge aus und wie beantrage ich ihn?
Published facts:
SEM: the State Secretariat for Migration is responsible for issuing travel documents and return visas to foreign nationals. The legal basis is the Ordinance of 14 November 2012 on the Issue of Travel Documents for Foreign Nationals (RDV, SR 143.5).
SEM issues travel documents for refugees under the Convention of 28 July 1951 relating to the Status of Refugees; passports for foreign nationals, for persons under the Convention of 28 September 1954 relating to the Status of Stateless Persons, for foreign nationals without documents who hold a residence permit B or a settlement permit C, and for persons with an F or N card who have grounds for travel or are leaving definitively; and return visas for provisionally admitted persons who hold a valid travel document of their home or origin state and have grounds for travel.
SEM: the travel documents it issues are immigration police documents. They prove neither the identity nor the nationality of the foreign national.
SEM: whoever wants to apply for a travel document must appear in person at the competent cantonal migration authority. Where a replacement for an expired travel document is applied for, the old document is handed to the cantonal migration authority for SEM, and the application should be filed with that authority six weeks before the old document expires or before the intended journey. A loss, including theft or complete destruction, must be reported to the local police station immediately; a loss abroad must also be reported to the competent Swiss diplomatic or consular representation.
SEM: a travel document for refugees and a passport for a foreign national under Article 4(1) RDV are valid for ten years when the person was 18 at the time of the application and for five years when they were not. SEM can set a shorter validity in particular circumstances, and the validity cannot be extended; after it expires the foreign national can apply for a new travel document.

Label: Renewing a residence permit
Description: Where to request a residence-permit renewal, which documents to enclose and when to apply, according to ch.ch.
Aliases: renew residence permit; extend permit; permit expires; Aufenthaltsbewilligung verlängern; Bewilligung verlängern; Ausweis läuft ab; Verlängerung; Aufenthaltsbewilligung; Wohnsitzgemeinde; aktuelle Bewilligung; Pass
Questions: When do I have to renew my B permit?; Wo verlängere ich meine Aufenthaltsbewilligung?; Which documents do I need to renew my residence permit?
Published facts:
ch.ch states that in some cantons a residence-permit renewal is requested directly from the cantonal authority; where the canton is not among them, the renewal is requested from the municipality of residence. The saved page does not name those cantons in its text.
ch.ch lists the documents to enclose with a renewal: the current permit; an identity card or valid passport of the country of origin, which for nationals of states outside the EU/EFTA must be valid at least three months longer than the permit; and the cantonal migration authority's notice that the permit expires, if one was received.
ch.ch states that a renewal application can be submitted at the earliest three months and must be submitted at the latest two weeks before the permit expires.

Label: Lost or stolen permit
Description: What to do when a permit card is lost or stolen, according to ch.ch.
Aliases: lost permit; stolen residence permit; permit card lost; Ausweis verloren; Bewilligung gestohlen; Ausländerausweis verloren; lost foreign national identity card; Verlustschein; Polizei; Einwohnerkontrolle; Duplikats; Passfoto
Questions: What do I do if I lose my residence permit?; Mein Ausweis wurde gestohlen, was muss ich tun?
Published facts:
ch.ch states that a lost or stolen permit is reported to the police, which issues a loss certificate. The holder then goes to the residents' office of the municipality (or to the cantonal migration authority) with the passport, a passport photo and the loss certificate, and pays for the duplicate or new permit, at a cost that varies. A permit that turns up again must be cancelled at the residents' office of the municipality of residence.

Label: Study admission under AIG Article 27
Description: Federal admission conditions for education and training, and what applies after studies end (AIG Art. 27).
Aliases: study in Switzerland; student residence permit; permit to study at a Swiss university; admission for studies; stay after my studies; Studium in der Schweiz; Bewilligung für das Studium; Aus- und Weiterbildung; Schulleitung; bedarfsgerechte Unterkunft; finanziellen Mittel; Minderjährigen; Betreuung; Zulassungsvoraussetzungen
Questions: What are the conditions for a residence permit to study at a Swiss university or school?; Welche Voraussetzungen gelten für eine Aufenthaltsbewilligung zum Studium in der Schweiz?
Published facts:
AIG Article 27 allows admission for education or further training when the school confirms admission, suitable accommodation and necessary funds are available, and the personal and educational prerequisites are met. Care must be ensured for minors.
After education is completed or discontinued, a further Swiss stay is governed by the AIG general admission conditions.

Label: Integration criteria and personal circumstances
Description: The federal integration criteria (public order, constitutional values, language, economic participation) and personal circumstances (AIG Art. 58a).
Aliases: integration criteria; integration requirements for a permit; how integration is assessed; well integrated; disability or illness and integration; Integrationsvoraussetzungen; gut integriert; Integrationskriterien; Beurteilung der Integration; öffentlichen Sicherheit und Ordnung; Werte der Bundesverfassung; Sprachkompetenzen; Wirtschaftsleben; Erwerb von Bildung; Behinderung oder Krankheit; gewichtigen persönlichen Umständen
Questions: Which criteria do the authorities use to judge whether a foreign national is integrated?; Was bedeutet Integration für meine Aufenthaltsbewilligung?
Published facts:
AIG Article 58a lists respect for public security and order, respect for Federal Constitution values, language skills, and participation in economic life or education as integration criteria.
Disability, illness or other weighty personal circumstances that prevent or hinder meeting the language and economic-participation or education criteria must be appropriately taken into account.

Label: Family reunification with a Swiss sponsor: Article 42(1)
Description: Family reunification with a Swiss citizen: entitlement of spouse and children under 18 (AIG Art. 42(1)).
Aliases: Familiennachzug Schweizer Ehegatte; mit Schweizerin verheiratet; mit Schweizer verheiratet; Ehefrau oder Ehemann eines Schweizer Bürgers; Schweizer Pass Ehepartner nachziehen; geheiratet; Schwiizer Pass; Schwiizerin; ghüratet; Art. 42 AIG; spouse of a Swiss citizen; married to a Swiss citizen; Swiss sponsor family reunification; Familienangehörige von Schweizerinnen und Schweizern; Ausländische Ehegatten; Ehegatten; ledige Kinder unter 18 Jahren; Schweizerinnen und Schweizern; Anspruch auf Erteilung und Verlängerung; zusammenwohnen
Questions: Ich habe den Schweizer Pass und habe einen Ausländer geheiratet. Bekommt mein Ehepartner eine Aufenthaltsbewilligung?; I am Swiss and married a foreigner. Is my spouse entitled to a residence permit?
Published facts:
Under AIG Article 42(1), foreign spouses and unmarried children under 18 of Swiss citizens are entitled to a residence permit and its renewal if they live with the Swiss family member.
ch.ch states that Swiss citizens can bring their spouse or registered partner and their unmarried children or grandchildren under 18. Children or grandchildren under 21 or dependent, and dependent parents and grandparents, can join when they hold an EU/EFTA residence permit; parents and grandparents are excluded while the Swiss citizen is in education.

Label: Family reunification with a settlement-permit sponsor
Description: Family reunification with a settlement-permit holder: entitlement and its conditions (AIG Art. 43).
Aliases: family reunification C permit holder; bring my family with a C permit; settlement permit family reunification; Familiennachzug C-Bewilligung; Familiennachzug mit Niederlassungsbewilligung C; Familie nachziehen C-Ausweis; Ehegatten und Kinder von Personen mit Niederlassungsbewilligung; Ehegatten; ledige Kinder unter 18 Jahren; Niederlassungsbewilligung; zusammenwohnen; bedarfsgerechte Wohnung; Sozialhilfe angewiesen; Landessprache; Ergänzungsleistungen; Familiennachzugs; Sprachförderungsangebot
Questions: I hold a settlement permit C. Under which conditions can my spouse and children come to live with me?; Welche Bedingungen gelten für den Nachzug von Ehegatten und Kindern mit einer C-Bewilligung?; Do my children also have to prove language skills when they join me on a C permit?
Published facts:
AIG Article 43(1) provides an entitlement for the foreign spouse and unmarried children under 18 of a settlement-permit holder if they live together, have suitable housing, do not depend on social assistance, meet the language condition, and the sponsor neither receives nor would become eligible for the specified annual supplementary benefits because of reunification.
For initial issuance under Article 43, enrolment in a language-support programme suffices instead of the language ability condition. That condition does not apply to unmarried children under 18.

Label: Family reunification with a residence-permit sponsor
Description: Family reunification with a residence-permit holder: discretionary issuance and its conditions (AIG Art. 44).
Aliases: Familiennachzug B-Bewilligung; Familiennachzug mit Aufenthaltsbewilligung B; Kind nachziehen B-Bewilligung; Ehepartner nachziehen B-Bewilligung; Art. 44 AIG; family reunification B permit holder; bring my child B permit; bring my spouse B permit; Ehegatten und Kinder von Personen mit Aufenthaltsbewilligung; Ehegatten; ledigen Kindern unter 18 Jahren; zusammenwohnen; bedarfsgerechte Wohnung; Sozialhilfe angewiesen; Ergänzungsleistungen; Familiennachzugs; Sprachförderungsangebot
Questions: Ich habe eine B-Bewilligung. Kann ich meine Frau und meine Kinder nachziehen?; I have a B permit. Can I bring my wife and children to Switzerland?
Published facts:
AIG Article 44(1) permits, rather than itself guarantees, issuance and renewal for the foreign spouse and unmarried children under 18 of a residence-permit holder if they live together, have suitable housing, do not depend on social assistance, meet the language condition, and the sponsor neither receives nor would become eligible for the specified annual supplementary benefits because of reunification.
For initial issuance under Article 44, language-course enrolment can replace the language ability condition. The condition does not apply to unmarried children under 18.

Label: Family reunification with an EU/EFTA sponsor
Description: Which family members EU/EFTA citizens living in Switzerland can bring, according to ch.ch.
Aliases: EU citizen family reunification; bring parents to Switzerland; Familiennachzug EU-Bürger; Eltern in die Schweiz holen; Kinder unter 21 nachziehen; EU/EFTA-Staatsbürgerschaft; Grosskinder; unterhaltsberechtigten Eltern und Grosseltern
Questions: Which family members can an EU citizen living in Switzerland bring?; Kann ich als EU-Bürgerin meine Eltern in die Schweiz holen?
Published facts:
ch.ch states that EU/EFTA citizens living in Switzerland can bring their spouse or registered partner, their children or grandchildren under 21 or dependent, and their dependent parents and grandparents; parents and grandparents are excluded while the EU/EFTA citizen is in education.

Label: AIG family-reunification deadlines
Description: Deadlines for claiming family reunification: five years, twelve months for children over twelve (AIG Art. 47).
Aliases: Nachzugsfrist; Frist Familiennachzug; Familiennachzug Frist verpasst; Kind über zwölf nachziehen; fünf Jahre Frist; zwölf Monate Frist; Art. 47 AIG; reunification deadline; child over twelve; late family reunification; deadline missed; Frist für den Familiennachzug; Familiennachzug; Anspruch auf Familiennachzug; fünf Jahren; Kinder über zwölf Jahre; zwölf Monaten nachgezogen; Fristen beginnen; Entstehung des Familienverhältnisses; nachträglicher Familiennachzug; wichtige familiäre Gründe; Kinder über 14 Jahre
Questions: Bis wann muss ich den Familiennachzug beantragen?; Mein Kind ist 13. Kann ich es noch nachziehen?; By when do I have to apply for family reunification?
Published facts:
AIG Article 47 sets a five-year deadline to claim family reunification, shortened to twelve months for children over twelve. These deadlines do not apply to the Article 42(2) route.
For Swiss family members under Article 42(1), the deadline starts with their entry or creation of the family relationship. For foreign sponsors, it starts with grant of the residence or settlement permit or creation of the family relationship.
Late family reunification is approved only when important family reasons are invoked. Children over fourteen are heard where necessary.

Label: Family reunification: relationship, housing, means and entry documents
Description: General conditions of family reunification on ch.ch: marriage or registered partnership, housing and means, and the documents family members need on entry.
Aliases: Familienzusammenführung; Familienzusammenführung beantragen; Ehegattennachzug; unmarried partner; girlfriend or boyfriend join Switzerland; Konkubinat Familiennachzug; Freundin in die Schweiz holen; documents for family reunification; Unterlagen Familiennachzug; Familiennachzug; eingetragenen Partnerschaft; Wohnung; Sozialhilfe; Identitätskarte; Sprachkurs; Niveau A1
Questions: Can I bring my unmarried partner to Switzerland?; Kann ich meinen Partner in die Schweiz holen, wenn wir nicht verheiratet sind?; What documents does my spouse need to enter Switzerland for family reunification?
Published facts:
ch.ch states that family reunification requires marriage or a registered partnership: an unmarried foreign partner cannot be brought to Switzerland, even by a Swiss citizen.
ch.ch states that bringing the whole family requires a home large enough by Swiss standards, because the family should in principle live together, and that the sponsor must not depend on social assistance; self-employed or non-working sponsors must prove sufficient funds to support the family.
ch.ch lists what family members need on entry: a valid identity card or passport; a visa where required; confirmation from the country of origin that the family relationship exists; for dependants, confirmation from the home or origin state of the maintenance obligation or of former cohabitation; and, if the spouse cannot communicate sufficiently in the local national language (at least oral level A1), confirmation of enrolment in a language course.

Label: Permit and work rights of reunited family members
Description: The permit type reunited family members receive and whether they may work, according to ch.ch.
Aliases: can my spouse work in Switzerland; family member work permit; Darf meine Frau in der Schweiz arbeiten; Erwerbstätigkeit Familienangehörige; which permit does my family get; Aufenthaltsbewilligung; Arbeitsbewilligung; Kurzaufenthaltsbewilligung; Grosseltern
Questions: Can my husband work after family reunification?; Welche Bewilligung bekommt meine Familie beim Familiennachzug?
Published facts:
ch.ch states that approved family members receive a residence permit whose type generally follows the sponsor's own permit. Family members may work in Switzerland, except parents and grandparents; only holders of a short-stay permit (L) must first apply for a work permit to the cantonal migration and labour-market authority.

Label: Residence after dissolution of family life
Description: Residence after the family relationship ends: three-year union with integration, or important personal reasons (AIG Art. 50).
Aliases: Trennung; Scheidung; getrennt; geschieden; Trennung Aufenthaltsbewilligung; Scheidung Aufenthaltsbewilligung; Ehe weniger als drei Jahre; Bewilligung nach Scheidung; Art. 50 AIG; separation; divorce; separating; end of marriage; permit after divorce; lose my permit; not married for three years; Auflösung der Familiengemeinschaft; Auflösung der Ehe; Ehegatten; Ehegemeinschaft mindestens drei Jahre; wichtige persönliche Gründe; Integrationskriterien

ch.ch states that the future employer takes the steps to obtain the work permit from the cantonal migration and labour-market authority, while a person planning self-employment must obtain the permit themselves.

Label: Third-country labour-market admission: the conditions
Description: The conditions SEM applies to admit a third-country worker: overall economic interest, priority of the domestic and EU/EFTA workforce, the duty to notify vacancies, customary pay and working conditions, personal qualifications and housing.
Aliases: work permit conditions third country; priority domestic workers; labour market test Switzerland; Vorrang Inländer Arbeitsbewilligung; Lohnbedingungen Arbeitsbewilligung; duales System; gesamtwirtschaftlichen Interesse; Vorrang; Stellenmeldepflicht; Regionalen Arbeitsvermittlungszentren; Gesamtarbeitsverträgen; qualifizierte Arbeitskräfte; bedarfsgerechte Wohnung
Questions: What does my employer have to prove before I can get a Swiss work permit as a third-country national?; Welche Voraussetzungen gelten für die Zulassung von Drittstaatsangehörigen zum Arbeitsmarkt?
Published facts:
SEM: Switzerland applies a dual system to the admission of foreign workers. Workers of all qualification levels from EU/EFTA states have simple access to the Swiss labour market through the free movement agreement, while admission from all other states, the third states, is complementary to it. The admission criteria are set out in the AIG and in the Ordinance on Admission, Residence and Gainful Employment and explained further in the AIG directives.
SEM: third-country nationals can be admitted to the Swiss labour market only where this serves Switzerland's overall economic interest, taking into account the labour-market situation, sustainable economic development and the ability of the foreign nationals to integrate. The applicant must give reasons for the overall economic interest and document it.
SEM: a third-country national can be admitted only when no person with priority is available on the domestic labour market or on the labour markets of the EU/EFTA states. Priority is enjoyed by Swiss citizens and by foreign nationals with a settlement permit or a residence permit. The employer must make credible search efforts that show, in timing, geographical breadth and content, a genuine attempt to fill the post with domestic or EU/EFTA candidates, and should contact third-country nationals only after such efforts have actually failed. Posts are in principle notified to the regional employment centres (RAV), an advertisement in the European Employment System (EURES) is also necessary, and the authorities must be shown that the search through the sector's specialist recruitment channels remained unsuccessful.
SEM: the duty to notify vacancies is a further admission condition next to the priority of the domestic workforce. It applies to the occupational groups, fields of activity or economic regions where the Swiss-wide unemployment rate reaches or exceeds 5 per cent; SECO sets the list of occupations concerned anew every year. Posts to be filled with third-country nationals in such occupations are subject to the duty unless an exception applies. The competent cantonal authority checks it, so employers attach proof of the notification to their permit applications in occupations with above-average unemployment.
SEM: the pay, the social insurance contributions and the working conditions of the foreign worker must correspond to what is customary for the place, the occupation and the sector; some sectors lay them down in collective employment agreements binding nationally or at least cantonally. The employer attaches to the application a written employment contract signed by both sides and marked "the contract applies only if the authorities grant a permit to work". Employers must register all employees with the social insurance institutions, and foreign workers without a settlement permit are taxed at source, so they are registered with the tax authorities and the employer deducts the tax from the wage monthly and transfers it.
SEM: managers, specialists and other qualified workers can be admitted. Qualified workers are in the first place persons with a university or university of applied sciences degree and several years of professional experience; depending on the occupation or specialisation, persons with particular professional training and several years of experience can also qualify. Besides the professional qualifications, integration criteria are taken into account: professional and social adaptability, language skills and age must make lasting integration into the Swiss labour market and society likely. The qualifications are checked against the CV, diplomas and references, of which the authorities need copies in the original language and translated into an official Swiss language or English.
SEM: certain deviations from the admission conditions are provided for by law. The most frequent cases are the transfer of senior managers and indispensable specialists within international companies, where priority does not apply; internships and further training in globally active companies and compulsory internships during studies; doctoral and post-doctoral researchers at a recognised Swiss university; family members of Swiss citizens, settled persons and residents, who need no separate permit procedure to work (family members of short-stay permit holders do); au pairs; and gainful employment after studies in Switzerland, where a person can be admitted without proof of priority if the work is of high scientific or economic interest, which applies only to degrees from recognised Swiss universities.
SEM: foreign nationals can be admitted for gainful employment only if they have housing that meets their needs.

The free-movement arrangement liberalises cross-border services for up to 90 effective working days per calendar year; the limit applies to both the posting enterprise and the posted person. Service provision exceeding 90 days needs a work permit and has no automatic entitlement.

Label: Zurich: working as a third-country national
Description: Canton of Zurich: the labour-market pre-decision of the Office for Economy, the steps from the employer's application to the permit card, and the short-term rules.
Aliases: work permit Zurich third country; who applies for a work permit in Zurich; labour market pre-decision Zurich; Arbeitsbewilligung Kanton Zürich Drittstaat; Amt für Wirtschaft Bewilligung; arbeitsmarktlichen Vorentscheid; Amt für Wirtschaft; EasyGov; duale Zulassungssystem; Einreiseerlaubnis; 8-Tage-Regelung
Questions: How does a work permit application work in the Canton of Zurich for a third-country national?; Wer stellt im Kanton Zürich das Gesuch für eine Arbeitsbewilligung?
Published facts:
Canton of Zurich: to work in Switzerland a third-country national needs a labour-market pre-decision, which the Office for Economy of the Canton of Zurich issues; the residence permit is then issued by the Migration Office.
Canton of Zurich: since 1 November 1998 the dual admission system applies, and the free movement agreement in force since 1 June 2002 eases admission from the EU/EFTA. Third-country nationals who want to work in Switzerland need a permit irrespective of the duration of their stay, to be applied for at the Office for Economy (AWI); work permits can be applied for through EasyGov, the online counter for businesses.
Canton of Zurich: the permit procedure runs in steps. The employer files the application for gainful employment with the Office for Economy (AWI); the AWI issues the labour-market pre-decision and forwards a positive one to the State Secretariat for Migration for approval; once SEM approves, the file goes to the Migration Office, which examines the application under immigration law and can still refuse the permit; if those conditions are met too, the Migration Office grants the permit to work. If the person is still abroad, the Migration Office authorises the Swiss representation to issue the visa by an entry authorisation, or, where there is no visa duty, issues an assurance of the permit to the employer. After entry the person registers in the municipality, where they are given an appointment to record their biometric data, appears in person at the Migration Office for it, and the card is produced and sent by post.
Canton of Zurich: the third-country spouse and the children (not yet 21 or entitled to maintenance) of an EU/EFTA national, and the spouses and children of Swiss citizens and of persons with a settlement or residence permit, may work irrespective of their own nationality.
Canton of Zurich: if a foreign national living outside the Canton of Zurich wants to work in the canton, the Migration Office issues a consent to gainful employment once the labour-market pre-decision arrives; in the reverse case the consent must be obtained from the canton of residence.
Canton of Zurich: besides the short-stay permit for contracts under a year and the residence permit for open-ended or longer contracts, shorter forms of employment exist. A person with an entry authorisation for work or a cross-border service of four months in total within 12 months does not have to register and needs no permit card. Under the eight-day rule no short-stay or residence permit is needed when a cross-border service or temporary work for a foreign employer lasts no longer than eight days in a calendar year; the rule does not apply in certain fields, among them hospitality and cleaning in businesses and households, where a permit is needed from the first day.

Label: Zurich: applying for the permit card and the biometrics appointment
Description: Canton of Zurich: how the credit-card format permit is applied for at the residents' registration office, what happens at the biometrics appointment, how to move it, and what to do when a card is lost.
Aliases: permit card appointment Zurich; biometrics appointment Zurich; move biometrics appointment; Ausländerausweis beantragen Zürich; Biometrietermin verschieben; Ausweis verloren Zürich; Kreditkartenformat; biometrischen Daten; ZEMIS; Einwohnerkontrolle; Biometrietermin; Token; Ausweisduplikates
Questions: How do I apply for my permit card in the Canton of Zurich and what happens at the biometrics appointment?; Wie kann ich meinen Biometrietermin beim Migrationsamt Zürich verschieben?
Published facts:
Canton of Zurich: both third-country nationals and EU/EFTA nationals receive a permit card in credit-card format. Switzerland has issued it since 12 December 2008 on the basis of the Schengen agreement, and since 24 January 2011 biometric data are stored on the cards of persons who are not nationals of EU or EFTA member states.
Canton of Zurich: a symbol on the top left of the card shows that it contains a chip with biometric data; the chip itself is not visible. The data are stored for five years in the central migration information system ZEMIS, solely so that a new card can be issued without recording them again. To have the biometric data recorded the person must come to the Migration Office in person and identify themselves; the appointment is given by the residents' registration office when they register.
Canton of Zurich: EU/EFTA nationals also receive a card in credit-card format, but unlike the card for third-country nationals it contains no chip with stored data. Persons with an F card (provisionally admitted persons) or an N card (asylum seekers) also receive their card in credit-card format, without a chip.
Canton of Zurich: the application for a permit or its extension is filed in person at the responsible residents' registration office in the canton. There the person is identified by their national passport, is given an appointment at the Migration Office to hand over the (biometric) data, and pays the fees under the cantonal fee ordinance. At the appointment the Migration Office records the signature and the facial image, and for third-country nationals two fingerprints, which are stored on the chip in the card. Minors must be accompanied by a parent with custody and persons under guardianship by their legal representative. After the data have been recorded and the permit granted, the card is produced by an external company and sent by post to the home address.
Canton of Zurich: an appointment for recording the data, given at the municipality, can be moved by the person themselves with the 16-digit token printed on the appointment confirmation; the new confirmation is printed and brought to the appointment. The loss of a C, B, L, N or F card must be reported to the police station of the municipality of residence, and in the city of Zurich to the "Ausweisverluste" office. For a duplicate the Migration Office recommends taking the original loss report and the passport to the residents' registration office.

Label: Zurich: entry permit for retirees and for close relatives in need of care
Description: Canton of Zurich: the two entry applications for third-country nationals without gainful employment, their conditions and the documents the Migration Office needs.
Aliases: retire in Switzerland third country; entry permit for elderly parents Zurich; move to Zurich as a pensioner; Einreisebewilligung Rentner Zürich; Einreisebewilligung nahe Verwandte; Einreisebewilligung; Mindestalter; besondere persönliche Beziehungen zur Schweiz; Betreuungs- oder Pflegebedürfnisse; Verpflichtungserklärung; Betreibungsregisterauszug
Questions: Can I move to Zurich as a retired non-EU citizen, and what does the Migration Office need?; Welche Unterlagen verlangt das Migrationsamt Zürich für die Einreise pflegebedürftiger Eltern?
Published facts:
Canton of Zurich Migration Office: an application for an entry permit to stay in Switzerland as a retiree can be examined when the minimum age for retirees of 55 has been reached, particular personal relations to Switzerland exist, and no gainful employment is pursued abroad apart from managing one's own assets.
Canton of Zurich Migration Office: for a retiree's entry application the documents are the completed entry application, the reasons for taking up residence in the Canton of Zurich and the municipality chosen, a detailed account of the relations to the canton (earlier stays proven by residence certificates of the residents' registration offices), a written confirmation that no gainful employment is pursued in Switzerland or abroad, proof of how living costs in Switzerland would be financed (monthly pensions, assets), a current criminal record extract from the home state with a certified German translation for applicants under 75 (or a certificate of good conduct where none can be obtained), and a written power of attorney with a German translation where the applicant is represented. The complete documents can be submitted at the counter, online or by post, and the examination can take several months.
Canton of Zurich Migration Office: an application for an entry permit for close relatives can be examined when there are particular needs of care or nursing, which is the case with physical or mental disabilities and with a serious illness, and when sufficient financial means can be shown.
Canton of Zurich Migration Office: for the entry application of a close relative the documents are the completed entry application, the reasons for and the place of the intended residence in the canton, who will provide the care where care is needed, the full personal details and addresses of all children, a health insurer's quotation for the monthly premiums of the compulsory basic insurance with a deductible of CHF 300 and copies of the premium statements of the family members, a written confirmation that no gainful employment is pursued, a copy of the lease of the person bringing the relative (with the landlord's written consent where the flat does not have the minimum size of the number of family members minus one or the occupancy would exceed the maximum in the lease), proof of how living costs would be financed, other financial obligations, a declaration of commitment for one year, copies of the last 12 pay slips or the tax bill, a current original debt enforcement register extract of the municipalities of residence of the last three years, and a written power of attorney where the applicant is represented. The complete documents can be submitted at the counter, online or by post, and the examination can take several months.

Questions: Under which conditions does Zurich examine the application of a retiree from outside the EU?; Welche Bedingungen gelten in Zürich für pensionierte Personen aus Drittstaaten?
Published facts:
Zurich states that retired third-country nationals have no entitlement to a permit. Applications are examined when the applicant is at least 55, has special personal ties to Switzerland and sufficient funds, and performs no gainful activity abroad except managing their own assets.

Label: Zurich: settlement permit after five years
Description: Canton of Zurich: who obtains the settlement permit C after five years instead of ten, the two country lists, and the German language proof.
Aliases: C permit after five years Zurich; five-year settlement permit Zurich; C-Bewilligung nach fünf Jahren Zürich; countries with a settlement agreement; Ehepartner Niederlassungsbewilligung fünf Jahre; fünf Jahre ununterbrochen; Integrationskriterien; besonderen Bestimmungen; Niederlassungsvereinbarung; Niederlassungsvertrag; Länder mit Niederlassungsvereinbarungen; Länder mit Niederlassungsverträgen; Deutschkenntnisse; Sprachnachweis
Questions: Which nationals can apply for the C permit after five years in Zurich?; Ich bin Italiener und wohne seit fünf Jahren in Zürich. Kann ich die Niederlassungsbewilligung beantragen?
Published facts:
The Canton of Zurich lists foreign spouses of settlement-permit holders among the persons who may obtain the settlement permit after five years instead of ten. They have a right to it when they have lived in Switzerland for five years without interruption, are well integrated and meet the integration criteria, no grounds for revocation are present, and the marriage still exists and is more than a formality when they apply; the page adds that the Swiss spouse holds a settlement permit during the five years of living together in Switzerland, and that a naturalisation in that time counts.
Foreign spouses and children of German, Austrian or Danish nationals have a right to a settlement permit in the Canton of Zurich when they have lived in Switzerland for five years without interruption, are well integrated and meet the integration criteria, no grounds for revocation are present, and the marriage is really lived when they apply.
Persons from countries with special provisions can obtain the settlement permit in the Canton of Zurich when they have lived in Switzerland for five years without interruption, are well integrated and meet the integration criteria, no grounds for revocation are present, and they come from a country with which Switzerland has signed a settlement agreement or a settlement treaty. Temporary stays such as education or further training, a cure or an internship do not, as a rule, count towards the five years.
The Canton of Zurich lists the countries with settlement agreements as: Belgium, Germany, Denmark, France, the Principality of Liechtenstein, Greece, Italy, the Netherlands, Austria, Portugal and Spain.
The Canton of Zurich lists the countries with settlement treaties as: Andorra, Finland, the United Kingdom, Ireland, Iceland, Canada, Luxembourg, Monaco, Norway, San Marino, Sweden, Vatican City and the United States of America.
Everyone applying for the settlement permit in the Canton of Zurich also submits evidence of German at level A2 spoken and A1 written at least. Persons from Germany, Austria and the Principality of Liechtenstein submit no language evidence.

For arrival from abroad, the City of Zurich requires an appointment and personal registration at Personenmeldeamt Zurich Sud. Without an appointment registration is not possible; for family registration every family member must attend in person.

The City of Zurich lists a passport (an identity card suffices for EU/EFTA nationals), rental or housing documentation, permit assurance and visa authorisation if available, an employment contract or study confirmation, applicable migration fees, and original civil-status documents for registration from abroad.

Published facts:
SEM states that EU/EFTA nationals taking up employment of more than three months must register with their municipality of residence and apply for a residence permit within 14 days of their arrival in Switzerland and before starting work. A valid identity card or passport and the employer's written confirmation of employment (for example the contract with its duration and workload) must be presented; the contract duration determines whether a short-stay permit L or a residence permit B is issued.
SEM states that the steps needed to obtain the residence permit can be completed after arrival in Switzerland.

Label: Compulsory health-insurance enrolment timing

Where Swiss compulsory health insurance applies, enrolment must occur within three months of the start of the obligation and is retroactive to that date, including the premiums.
With late enrolment, coverage starts only on joining; an inexcusable delay incurs a premium surcharge.

Label: Agreement on the Free Movement of Persons (FZA): aims and principles
Description: The Switzerland-EU Agreement on the Free Movement of Persons (FZA, SR 0.142.112.681): its aims, non-discrimination, the public-order limit and the duty to report presence.
Aliases: Agreement on the Free Movement of Persons; free movement of persons Switzerland EU; AFMP; FZA; ALCP; bilateral agreement free movement; Personenfreizügigkeit; Freizügigkeitsabkommen Schweiz EU; Freizügigkeit; Nichtdiskriminierung; öffentlichen Ordnung; Anwesenheit
Questions: What does the free movement agreement between Switzerland and the EU guarantee?; Was regelt das Freizügigkeitsabkommen?
Published facts:
The Agreement between Switzerland and the European Community and its member states on the free movement of persons (FZA, SR 0.142.112.681) was concluded on 21 June 1999 and entered into force on 1 June 2002. Article 1 states its aims for nationals of the EU member states and Switzerland: a right of entry, residence, access to employment, establishment as a self-employed person and a right to remain; easier provision of services, in particular short-term services; entry and residence for persons not in gainful employment; and the same living, employment and working conditions as for nationals.
FZA Article 2: nationals of a contracting party who reside lawfully in the territory of another contracting party must not be discriminated against on grounds of nationality in the application of the agreement under its Annexes I, II and III.
FZA Annex I Article 5(1): the rights granted by the agreement may be restricted only by measures justified on grounds of public order, public security or public health.
FZA Annex I Article 2(4): the contracting parties may require nationals of the other contracting parties to report their presence in their territory.

Label: FZA: entry with an identity card or passport
Description: Entry of EU nationals, their family members and posted workers on a valid identity card or passport, and when a visa may still be required (FZA Annex I Art. 1).
Aliases: enter Switzerland with ID card; EU citizen visa Switzerland; visa for family member of EU citizen; Einreise mit Personalausweis; Visum Familienangehörige EU-Bürger; Einreise und Ausreise; Personalausweises oder Reisepasses; Einreisevisum; entsandten Arbeitnehmern
Questions: Does an EU citizen need a visa to enter Switzerland?; Does my non-EU spouse need a visa to join me in Switzerland?; Reicht an der Grenze ein EU-Personalausweis?
Published facts:
FZA Annex I Article 1(1): Switzerland and the EU member states allow nationals of the other contracting parties, their family members and posted workers to enter on presentation of a valid identity card or passport. No entry visa or equivalent may be required, except for family members and posted workers who are not nationals of a contracting party; they are to be given every facility to obtain any visa they need.

Label: FZA: staying to look for work
Description: The treaty right of EU nationals to stay in Switzerland for up to six months to look for work (FZA Annex I Art. 2(1)).
Aliases: look for work EU citizen treaty; job search six months; Stellensuche sechs Monate; Arbeitsuche Freizügigkeitsabkommen; Beschäftigung zu suchen; sechs Monaten; Arbeitsuchenden; Arbeitsämter; Sozialhilfe
Questions: How long may an EU citizen stay in Switzerland to look for a job under the free movement agreement?; Wie lange darf ich aus der EU zur Stellensuche einreisen und bleiben?
Published facts:
FZA Annex I Article 2(1): nationals of a contracting party may go to another contracting party, or stay there after an employment of less than one year ends, to look for work, and may stay for a reasonable period of up to six months where this is needed to learn of job offers matching their qualifications and to take steps to be hired. Jobseekers are entitled to the same help from the employment offices as that state's own nationals, and may be excluded from social assistance during that stay.

Label: FZA: residence permit of an EU employee
Description: Validity, renewal, documents and protection of the residence permit of an employed EU national by contract length (FZA Annex I Art. 6).
Aliases: EU employee residence permit validity; five-year permit EU worker; permit after losing job EU citizen; Aufenthaltserlaubnis fünf Jahre; Arbeitslosigkeit Aufenthaltsbewilligung EU; Aufenthaltsregelung; Aufenthaltserlaubnis; Gültigkeitsdauer; fünf Jahren; unfreiwillig arbeitslos; Einstellungserklärung; Arbeitsbescheinigung; Aufenthaltsunterbrechungen
Questions: How long is the residence permit of an EU citizen with a permanent job valid?; Can an EU citizen lose the residence permit after becoming unemployed?; Which documents may the authorities ask from an EU worker for the permit?; Wie lange ist die Aufenthaltsbewilligung eines EU-Arbeitnehmers mit unbefristeter Stelle gültig?
Published facts:
FZA Annex I Article 6(1): an employed national of a contracting party with an employment relationship of at least one year with an employer in the host state receives a residence permit valid for at least five years from its issue, which is automatically extended by at least five years. At the first extension its validity may be limited, but not to less than one year, if the holder has been involuntarily unemployed for more than twelve consecutive months.
FZA Annex I Article 6(2): an employee with an employment relationship of more than three months and less than one year receives a residence permit valid for the duration of the employment contract; an employee whose employment lasts at most three months needs no residence permit.
FZA Annex I Article 6(3): to issue the residence permit, the contracting parties may require the employee to present only the identity document used to enter and a declaration of engagement from the employer or a certificate of employment.
FZA Annex I Article 6(4)-(5): the residence permit is valid for the whole territory of the issuing state; breaks in residence of up to six consecutive months and absence for military service do not affect its validity.
FZA Annex I Article 6(6): a valid residence permit may not be withdrawn from an employee solely because the employee no longer has work, either because of temporary incapacity for work from illness or accident, or because of involuntary unemployment duly confirmed by the competent employment office.

Label: FZA: changing job, employer, profession or place
Description: The treaty right of EU employees and self-employed persons to change employer, job, profession, status and place of work and residence (FZA Annex I Art. 8 and 14).
Aliases: change employer EU citizen treaty; switch from employee to self-employed EU citizen; move to another canton EU citizen; Berufliche Mobilität; Wechsel des Arbeitgebers; Berufliche und geographische Mobilität; Aufenthaltsortes; selbstständigen Erwerbstätigkeit
Questions: May an EU citizen become self-employed on an employee permit?; Can an EU citizen move to another canton without a new permit?; Darf ich als Arbeitnehmer aus der EU die Stelle, den Beruf oder den Wohnkanton wechseln?
Published facts:
FZA Annex I Article 8: employees have the right to occupational and geographical mobility throughout the host state. Occupational mobility covers changing employer, job or occupation and moving from employment to self-employment; geographical mobility covers changing the place of work and of residence.
FZA Annex I Article 14: self-employed persons have the right to occupational and geographical mobility throughout the host state, covering a change of occupation and a move from self-employment to employment, and a change of the place of work and of residence.

Label: FZA: residence permit of a self-employed EU national
Description: The five-year residence permit of a self-employed EU national, its renewal, the documents that may be required and its protection (FZA Annex I Art. 12).
Aliases: self-employed EU citizen permit treaty; freelancer permit five years; Selbstständige Aufenthaltserlaubnis; selbständig erwerbend EU Freizügigkeit; Selbstständige; niedergelassen; selbstständige Erwerbstätigkeit; Aufenthaltserlaubnis; Arbeitsunfähigkeit
Questions: What does an EU citizen need to show to get a permit as a self-employed person?; Was muss ich nachweisen, um als Selbständiger aus der EU eine Aufenthaltsbewilligung zu erhalten?
Published facts:
FZA Annex I Article 12(1)-(2): a national of a contracting party who wishes to settle in another contracting party to pursue a self-employed activity receives a residence permit valid for at least five years from its issue, provided the person shows the competent national authorities that they are established or wish to establish themselves for that purpose. The permit is automatically extended by at least five years if the person shows that they are pursuing a self-employed activity.
FZA Annex I Article 12(3): to issue the permit, the contracting parties may require from a self-employed person only the identity document used to enter and the proof described in paragraphs 1 and 2.
FZA Annex I Article 12(4)-(6): the permit is valid for the whole territory of the issuing state; breaks in residence of up to six consecutive months and absence for military service do not affect its validity; and a valid permit may not be withdrawn solely because the person has stopped working owing to temporary incapacity for work from illness or accident.

Label: FZA: cross-border commuters
Description: Who is an employed or self-employed cross-border commuter under the treaty, and the special certificate instead of a residence permit (FZA Annex I Art. 7 and 13).
Aliases: cross-border commuter; frontier worker; Grenzgänger; cross-border permit G; Grenzgängerbewilligung; pendeln; Pendler; commute daily from a neighbouring country; Sonderbescheinigung; Wohnort; einmal in der Woche
Questions: Does a cross-border commuter from the EU need a residence permit?; Welche Bewilligung braucht ein Grenzgänger, der täglich in seinen Wohnstaat zurückkehrt?
Published facts:
FZA Annex I Article 7: an employed cross-border commuter is a national of a contracting party resident in one contracting party who works as an employee in the other and as a rule returns home daily or at least once a week. Such commuters need no residence permit; the employing state may issue a special certificate valid for at least five years, or for the duration of the employment if that is more than three months and less than one year, renewed by at least five years if the commuter shows they are working. The certificate is valid for the whole territory of the issuing state.
FZA Annex I Article 13: a self-employed cross-border commuter is a national of a contracting party resident in one contracting party who is self-employed in the other and as a rule returns home daily or at least once a week. Such commuters need no residence permit; the state concerned may issue a special certificate valid for at least five years if they show they are or wish to be self-employed, renewed by at least five years if they show they are self-employed. The certificate is valid for the whole territory of the issuing state.

Label: FZA: family members of an EU national
Description: Which family members of an EU national may join them regardless of nationality, the documents that may be required, the permit's validity and the family members' right to work (FZA Annex I Art. 3).
Aliases: family reunification free movement agreement; family members EU citizen any nationality; non-EU spouse of EU citizen; Familiennachzug Freizügigkeitsabkommen; Familienangehörige Drittstaat; Familienangehörige; Wohnung zu nehmen; Verwandten in absteigender Linie; Unterhalt gewährt; ungeachtet ihrer Staatsangehörigkeit; Verwandtschaftsverhältnis; häuslichen Gemeinschaft
Questions: Can the non-EU wife of an EU citizen living in Zurich work?; Which family members can an EU citizen bring to Switzerland?; Which documents may be required for the permit of an EU citizen's family member?; Welche Familienangehörigen dürfen mit einem EU-Arbeitnehmer zusammenwohnen?
Published facts:
FZA Annex I Article 3(1): the family members of a national of a contracting party who has a right of residence have the right to take up residence with that person. An employee must have housing for the family that meets the normal requirements for national workers in the region of employment; this must not lead to discrimination between national workers and workers from the other contracting party.
FZA Annex I Article 3(2): regardless of their nationality, family members are the spouse and the descendants who are under 21 or dependent; the dependent relatives in the ascending line of the person and of the spouse; and, for students, the spouse and the dependent children. The contracting parties are to favour the admission of any other family member who is dependent on the national or lived in the national's household in the country of origin.
FZA Annex I Article 3(3): for a family member's residence permit, the contracting parties may require only the identity document used to enter; a certificate from the competent authority of the state of origin confirming the relationship; and, for dependants, a certificate from that authority confirming that the national supports them or that they live in the national's household in that state.
FZA Annex I Article 3(4)-(5): a family member's residence permit has the same validity as that of the person from whom the right derives; the spouse and the children under 21 or dependent of a person with a right of residence have the right to take up gainful employment, regardless of their nationality.

Label: FZA: residence without gainful employment
Description: Residence permits of EU nationals who do not work, such as retirees, students and persons after a short job: sufficient means, health insurance, validity (FZA Annex I Art. 24).
Aliases: retire to Switzerland EU citizen; EU pensioner Switzerland; EU student permit Switzerland; sufficient financial means; Nichterwerbstätige EU; Rentner EU Aufenthalt Schweiz; Studierende EU Aufenthaltsbewilligung; keine Erwerbstätigkeit; ausreichende finanzielle Mittel; Krankenversicherungsschutz; sämtliche Risiken; Fürsorgeleistungen; Mindestrente; Arbeitslosengeld; Studierenden; anerkannten Lehranstalt
Questions: Can an EU pensioner live in Switzerland without working?; What does an EU student need for a Swiss residence permit?; How much money does an EU citizen need to live in Switzerland without a job?; Welche Mittel und welche Krankenversicherung muss ich als Rentnerin oder Student aus der EU nachweisen?
Published facts:
FZA Annex I Article 24(1): a national of a contracting party who does not work in the host state and has no right of residence under another provision of the agreement receives a residence permit valid for at least five years, provided they show the competent national authorities that they have, for themselves and their family members, sufficient financial means not to need social assistance during their stay, and health insurance covering all risks. The contracting parties may require the permit to be renewed after the first two years of residence if they consider it necessary.
FZA Annex I Article 24(2): financial means are sufficient if they exceed the amount below which the host state's own nationals, given their personal situation and that of their family members, are entitled to welfare benefits; where that test cannot be applied, they are sufficient if they exceed the minimum pension paid by the host state's social insurance.
FZA Annex I Article 24(3): persons who held an employment of less than one year in a contracting party may stay there if they meet the conditions of paragraph 1; the unemployment benefit they are entitled to counts as financial means.
FZA Annex I Article 24(4)-(5): a student without a right of residence under another provision of the agreement receives a residence permit limited to the duration of the training, or to one year if the training lasts longer, provided the student is enrolled at a recognised institution mainly for vocational training, has health insurance covering all risks, and makes credible by a declaration or equivalent means of their choice that they, their spouse and their dependent children will not need the host state's social assistance. The student's permit is extended every year for the remaining duration of the training; the agreement governs neither access to education nor maintenance grants.
FZA Annex I Article 24(5)-(8): the residence permit of a person without gainful employment is automatically extended by at least five years as long as the conditions are met; breaks in residence of up to six consecutive months and absence for military service do not affect its validity; it is valid for the whole territory of the issuing state; and the right of residence lasts as long as the conditions of paragraph 1 are met.

Label: FZA: cross-border services up to 90 working days
Description: The treaty's 90-working-day rule for cross-border services by EU service providers and posted workers, their residence, the exceptions, and service recipients (FZA Art. 5, Annex I Art. 17 to 23).
Aliases: 90 days service provision treaty; posted workers free movement agreement; service recipient Switzerland; temporary staffing agency EU; Dienstleistungserbringer; Entsendung Freizügigkeitsabkommen; Personalverleih EU; 90 Arbeitstage pro Kalenderjahr; 90 tatsächliche Arbeitstage; entsandt; Arbeitsvermittlungs- und -verleihunternehmen; Finanzdienstleistungen; Dienstleistungsempfänger
Questions: How many days per year may an EU company provide services in Switzerland?; Can an EU temporary staffing agency post workers to Switzerland under the free movement agreement?; Does a posted worker from a non-EU country need a permit to work on an assignment in Switzerland?; Wie viele Arbeitstage im Jahr darf eine Firma aus der EU hier Dienstleistungen erbringen?
Published facts:
FZA Article 5(1) and Annex I Article 21(1): service providers, including companies, have the right to provide services in the territory of the other contracting party for an actual duration of no more than 90 working days per calendar year; continuous and successive services count together.
FZA Annex I Article 17: for services under Article 5 it is prohibited to restrict cross-border services of no more than 90 actual working days per calendar year, and to restrict the entry and residence of service providers who are nationals of an EU member state or Switzerland established in a contracting party other than that of the service recipient, and of employees of a service provider, whatever their nationality, who are integrated into the regular labour market of a contracting party and posted to provide a service.
FZA Annex I Article 20(1)-(3): persons entitled to provide services under Annex I Article 17(b) need no residence permit for stays of up to 90 days, and the identity document they entered with also covers their stay; those entitled to provide services for more than 90 days, or authorised to do so, receive a residence permit valid for the duration of the service. The right of residence covers the whole of Switzerland or of the EU member state concerned.
FZA Annex I Article 22(2)-(4): the services rules leave untouched the laws on working and employment conditions of posted workers (with reference to Directive 96/71/EC); the laws in force when the agreement entered into force on the activities of employment and temporary-staffing agencies and on financial services that require prior authorisation; and rules on services of up to 90 actual working days that are justified by overriding reasons of general interest.
FZA Annex I Article 23(1): a person who goes to another contracting party only as the recipient of a service needs no residence permit for stays of up to three months; for longer stays they receive a permit valid for the duration of the service, and they may be excluded from social assistance during their stay.

Label: FZA: right to remain after working
Description: The treaty right of EU nationals and their family members to remain in Switzerland after their gainful activity ends (FZA Annex I Art. 4).
Aliases: right to remain after retirement EU citizen; stay in Switzerland after retiring EU; Verbleiberecht; nach der Pensionierung in der Schweiz bleiben EU; Beendigung ihrer Erwerbstätigkeit
Questions: Can an EU citizen stay in Switzerland after retiring from a Swiss job?; Habe ich ein Verbleiberecht, wenn meine Erwerbstätigkeit endet?
Published facts:
FZA Annex I Article 4(1): nationals of a contracting party and their family members have a right to remain in the territory of the other contracting party after their gainful activity ends.

Label: FZA: equal treatment at work
Description: Equal treatment of EU employees and self-employed persons with Swiss nationals in pay, dismissal, tax and social advantages, and the public-administration exception (FZA Annex I Art. 9, 10 and 15).
Aliases: equal pay EU worker Switzerland; discrimination EU citizen at work; public service job EU citizen; Gleichbehandlung; Beamtenstelle EU-Bürger; Entlohnung; Kündigung; steuerlichen und sozialen Vergünstigungen; öffentlichen Verwaltung; hoheitlicher Befugnisse
Questions: Can a Swiss employer pay an EU worker less than a Swiss worker?; Can an EU citizen work for the Swiss public administration?; Darf mir ein Arbeitgeber wegen meiner EU-Staatsangehörigkeit weniger Lohn zahlen?
Published facts:
FZA Annex I Article 9(1)-(2): an employed national of a contracting party may not be treated differently from national workers because of nationality in conditions of employment and work, in particular pay, dismissal and, after becoming unemployed, reinstatement or re-employment. The employee and the family members enjoy the same tax and social advantages as national workers and their family members.
FZA Annex I Article 10: an employed national of a contracting party may be refused employment in the public administration where it involves the exercise of public authority and serves to safeguard the general interests of the state or other public bodies.
FZA Annex I Article 15: self-employed persons receive treatment no less favourable than the host state's own nationals regarding access to and pursuit of a self-employed activity, and Annex I Article 9 applies to them by analogy.
