Published facts:
City of Zurich: residents of the City of Zurich complete marriage preparation with the City's Zivilstandsamt even if the wedding itself will take place outside the city; residents of another place contact the civil registry office of their own place of residence instead.
City of Zurich: to arrange marriage preparation, a couple where at least one partner has a foreign passport fills in the City's contact form, while a couple where both partners have a Swiss passport calls the Zivilstandsamt (+41 44 412 31 50) three months before the wedding date to book the appointment.
City of Zurich: both partners need good German or English skills for marriage preparation, including understanding what is said, asking and understanding answers to questions, and reading and understanding forms and documents in German or English; a partner who lacks this needs an interpreter (Dolmetschhilfe), which costs Fr. 165 and is paid directly at the appointment by credit or debit card or Twint.
City of Zurich: at the marriage preparation appointment, a Swiss citizen shows a passport or identity card plus a certificate of residence if living outside the canton of Zurich; a foreign national without a Swiss passport shows a passport or identity card plus proof of their residence status, such as a foreign nationals' ID (Ausländerausweis) or visa, and likewise a certificate of residence if living outside the canton of Zurich.
City of Zurich: for marriage preparation and the wedding, a person must be legally resident in Switzerland; without a lawful stay, such as a visa or a foreign nationals' ID (Ausländerausweis), a person cannot marry in Switzerland.
City of Zurich: a couple where at least one partner has a foreign passport must send the required original documents from their home country to the Zivilstandesamt of the City of Zurich (Postfach, 8022 Zurich) at the latest 2 months before the wedding; only once all required documents have been submitted does the City send the link to book the marriage preparation appointment, at the earliest 3 months before the wedding date.
City of Zurich: obtaining the documents needed from the authorities of the home country or country of birth can take between 3 days and 6 months, so a couple should not book their wedding date too tightly.
City of Zurich: marriage preparation must be completed at the latest 1 month before the chosen wedding date, otherwise the reservation is cancelled.
City of Zurich: which documents are needed for the wedding depends on the couple's civil status, country of birth, and nationality; if either partner does not have a Swiss passport, the City of Zurich advises individually on the necessary documents after the couple fills in its contact form.

Label: Deregistering when leaving the City of Zurich
Description: City of Zurich procedure to deregister (Wegzug) when moving to another municipality, ending a weekly residence, or moving abroad, and what the City's Tax Office requires from someone leaving before they stop being taxed in the city. [City of Zurich]
Aliases: moving away from Zurich; deregistering when leaving Zurich; Wegzug melden; moving abroad from Zurich; Steuern bei Wegzug ins Ausland; deregistration confirmation cost; Abmeldebestätigung Kosten; appointment to deregister in Zurich; eUmzug; tax office when leaving Switzerland; Abmeldung Wegzug; Wegzug; Abmeldeerklärung; Personenmeldeamt; Wochenaufenthalt; Abmeldebestätigung; Wohnsitzattest; Steueramt; Steuerpflicht; Quellensteuer
Questions: How do I deregister when I move away from Zurich, and what is the deadline?; What happens to my taxes if I move abroad from Zurich?; Was muss ich beim Wegzug ins Ausland bei der Stadt Zürich erledigen, und was passiert mit meinen Steuern?
Published facts:
City of Zurich: report your departure within 14 days after moving out; the report can be filed at the earliest 30 days before the planned move.
City of Zurich: departure can be reported online or in person; a move to another Swiss municipality is reported online via eUmzug, while a move abroad is reported by submitting the deregistration declaration (Abmeldeerklärung) through the contact form.
City of Zurich: to end a weekly residence (Wochenaufenthalt) and move back to the main domicile, submit the deregistration declaration through the contact form; it must be filled in completely and signed.
City of Zurich: if reporting online is not possible, departure can be reported in person at the Personenmeldeamt Zurich Nord or Zurich West, but this requires a booked appointment; the appointment can be booked at the earliest 30 days before the planned move, and if the booked appointment falls more than 30 days before the planned move, it cannot be processed and a new appointment must be arranged.
City of Zurich: for the in-person appointment, bring a passport or ID card, and foreign nationals also bring their foreign nationals' ID (Ausländerausweis); a written deregistration confirmation (Abmeldebestätigung) costs Fr. 20, preferably paid by card.
City of Zurich: when a minor child moves away with only one parent, the signature of the departing parent is enough for a move within Switzerland, but a move abroad requires the signatures of both parents, along with copies of their identity documents.
City of Zurich: after deregistration, a deregistration confirmation (Abmeldebestätigung) or certificate of residence (Wohnsitzattest) can be ordered in the webshop; it may be needed to cancel contracts such as health insurance or bank accounts, for tax matters, to re-register vehicles, to apply for social benefits or pensions abroad, or to export household goods.
City of Zurich: moving abroad ends tax liability in the City of Zurich, and at the same time all taxes, including provisional ones, become due for payment; contact the City's Tax Office (Steueramt) to discuss the next steps, or visit its counter right after deregistering at the Personenmeldeamt.
City of Zurich: a person moving abroad must appoint an authorised tax representative with a registered office or residence in Switzerland if their taxes cannot be finally assessed before departure, if they are subject to a subsequent ordinary assessment of tax at source, if a limited tax liability in Switzerland continues (property or permanent establishment), or if they remain employed by the Confederation or another Swiss public-law body.

Label: Zurich: finding integration offers and German courses
Description: The cantonal offer database, the free German-course advice in 16 languages, the cantonal German-course database, and the separate offers of the cities of Zurich and Winterthur.
Aliases: integration offers Zurich; German courses in the Canton of Zurich; where to find a German course; language course database Zurich; Deutschkurs finden Kanton Zürich; Integrationsangebote Kanton Zürich; Angebotsdatenbank; Fachstelle Integration; Deutschkursberatung; Deutschkurs-Datenbank; Sprachprüfungen; Begrüssungsgespräche; Spielgruppen mit Sprachbildung; Wohngemeinde
Questions: Where do I find a German course or an integration offer in the Canton of Zurich?; Wo finde ich einen Deutschkurs im Kanton Zürich?
Published facts:
The Fachstelle Integration of the Canton of Zurich runs an offer database of the integration offers that the canton finances together with the municipalities from the federal integration credit; to find an offer a user selects a category and their municipality of residence in the search mask and opens the details of an entry. The page names welcome talks for newcomers, German courses and playgroups with integrated language support as examples of what many municipalities offer.
Many municipalities in the Canton of Zurich have contact persons for integration who also give advice on German courses; where the municipality of residence offers no such advice, residents can turn to the cantonal German-course advice, which is free and available in 16 languages. The canton also keeps a German-course database listing German courses and language examinations in the Canton of Zurich, and the page states that language examinations matter for the residence permit, for naturalisation and for education and work.
The cities of Zurich and Winterthur keep their own offer databases, which the cantonal page links separately: German courses and the moving-from-abroad pages of the City of Zurich, and the infoDesk / welcomeDesk and German courses of the City of Winterthur.

Label: Zurich: first information and counselling for newcomers
Description: Who informs people newly arrived from abroad in the Canton of Zurich, who is pointed to offers early, and the counselling organisations the canton lists.
Aliases: first information for newcomers Zurich; who informs newcomers in the canton; counselling for migrants Zurich; advice centres for migrants; Erstinformation Kanton Zürich; Beratungsstellen für Migrantinnen und Migranten; Willkommen im Kanton Zürich; Erstinformation; neu Zugezogene; Integrationsangebote; Beratungsstellen; Fachstelle Integration; Familiennachzug; Integrationsförderbedarf
Questions: Who informs me about living in the Canton of Zurich after I arrive from abroad?; Wer informiert neu zugezogene Personen im Kanton Zürich?
Published facts:
The Canton of Zurich states as an aim of its integration programme that everyone newly arrived from abroad is welcomed in Switzerland and informed about the most important living conditions and integration offers, and that personally conveyed and multilingual information is central so that newcomers can orient themselves and settle in quickly at their new place of residence.
In the Canton of Zurich it is first of all the municipalities that inform newly arrived migrants as soon as possible after their arrival about the local living conditions, give them a first orientation at their new place of residence and, where needed, arrange access to German courses and other integration offers. The Fachstelle Integration provides the municipalities with a guide for planning and running first-information offers, which also addresses municipalities that do not take part in the cantonal integration programme.
People with a particular need for integration support should be pointed to suitable offers as early as possible; the canton names three groups in particular: persons in family reunification, persons threatened by or affected by poverty, and persons with training and skilled-worker potential.
For further information, migrants can use the topic-specific counselling of the regular services or migration-specific counselling offers. The Fachstelle Integration provides authorities, institutions and private persons with a list of organisations that offer migration-specific and topic-specific counselling in the Canton of Zurich; the organisations on it show expertise in counselling different target groups and follow recognised quality standards. The Fachstelle updates the list at least once a year and states that it makes no claim to completeness; further offers can be reported to integration@ji.zh.ch.
The Canton of Zurich publishes information for a good start at the new place of residence on its page "Willkommen im Kanton Zürich", with links to further information and to suitable information points.

Label: Zurich: protection from racist discrimination
Description: What the Canton of Zurich says racist discrimination is, the counselling centre ZüRAS, the national bodies and reporting platforms, and the legal bases.
Aliases: racism counselling Zurich; where to report racist discrimination; discrimination because of origin or religion; ZüRAS; Rassismus Beratung Kanton Zürich; rassistische Diskriminierung melden; rassistische Diskriminierung; Anlaufstelle; Beratungsnetz für Rassismusopfer; Fachstelle für Rassismusbekämpfung; Eidgenössischen Kommission gegen Rassismus; Mehrfachdiskriminierung; Herabsetzung
Questions: Where can I get advice in the Canton of Zurich if I experience racist discrimination?; Wohin kann ich mich im Kanton Zürich wenden, wenn ich rassistisch diskriminiert werde?
Published facts:
The Canton of Zurich describes racist discrimination as acts that demean people because of their skin colour, their origin, their language, their ethnic-cultural belonging or their religion, and names demeaning statements, exclusion, refusal of a service and violence as forms of it. It states that racism can be structural, can happen intentionally or unintentionally, can occur together with discrimination on other grounds, and can occur at work, when looking for a flat or at school; people with a Swiss passport can experience it too.
The Zurich counselling centre against racism, ZüRAS, advises people who experience racist discrimination. Counselling is possible in several languages and is free for people who live in the Canton of Zurich. ZüRAS is run by the Asylorganisation Zürich (AOZ) on behalf of the canton and the city.
Besides the counselling and specialist offices in the Canton of Zurich, the page names two further places for cases of racism in Switzerland: the reporting platform for online racism, where cases of hate speech on the internet and in social media can be reported (www.reportonlineracism.ch), and the counselling network for victims of racism, a network of specialist offices across Switzerland that advise in cases of racism (www.network-racism.ch).
The federal Service for Combating Racism is responsible for preventing racism and coordinates activities at national, cantonal and communal level, and has published a monitoring report on racist discrimination in Switzerland every two years since 2012, available online since 2024. The Federal Commission against Racism advises, produces publications and carries out prevention, and its online legal guide explains the legal situation and includes a glossary of the most important terms. The foundation against racism and antisemitism GRA records racist and antisemitic incidents across Switzerland.
The Canton of Zurich names three legal bases for protection from racist discrimination: the Federal Constitution, which since 2000 holds as a fundamental right in Article 8 paragraph 2 that nobody may be discriminated against because of origin, "race", language, way of life or religious conviction, a right the Zurich cantonal constitution has held since 2005; the Criminal Code, which in Article 261bis punishes certain discriminating acts committed in public, including the public demeaning of persons or groups because of their "race", ethnicity or religion, hate speech and calls for violence against them, and the refusal of a service offered to the general public on one of those grounds; and the Foreign Nationals and Integration Act, which since 2019 holds in Article 53 that the Confederation, the cantons and the communes take account of the concerns of integration and of protection from discrimination when performing their tasks.
For discrimination on other grounds the Canton of Zurich names other offices than the Fachstelle Integration: discrimination because of sex or sexual orientation belongs to the Fachstelle Gleichstellung, and discrimination because of a disability to the Koordinationsstelle Behindertenrechte.

Label: Zurich: platform for migrant associations
Description: The cantonal platform on which migrant and religious associations of the Canton of Zurich can be found and can register, and the Migrazin newsletter.
Aliases: migrant associations Zurich; find an association of my country; platform for migrant associations; Migrantenvereine Kanton Zürich; migrantische Vereine; Migrazin; Plattform für Migrantenvereine; migrantische; Vernetzung; Fachstelle Integration
Questions: How do I find an association of migrants from my country in the Canton of Zurich?; Wie finde ich einen migrantischen Verein im Kanton Zürich?
Published facts:
The Fachstelle Integration of the Canton of Zurich runs a platform for migrant associations on which migrant and religious associations active in the canton can be searched by various criteria, for example by municipality or region, and on which associations can register themselves. The canton launched the platform at the beginning of 2015 to strengthen networking and ease the flow of information, and states that migrant and religious associations inform, advise and enable exchange, mostly as voluntary work.
With the newsletter Migrazin the Fachstelle Integration sends information from the Canton of Zurich to migrant and religious associations; associations that want to receive it write to the Fachstelle to sign up, and earlier issues can be viewed on the page.
The Fachstelle Integration names a contact person for migrant organisations; on the access date of the page this was Deniz Yüksel, deniz.yueksel@ji.zh.ch, +41 43 259 25 27.

Label: Zurich: funding for integration projects
Description: The Canton of Zurich's contributions to integration projects under the cantonal integration programme KIP 3, who may apply, the two funding priorities, the amounts and the deadlines.
Aliases: funding for an integration project Zurich; money for a project with migrants; project contribution integration canton Zurich; Projektförderung Integration Kanton Zürich; Gesuch Integrationsprojekt; Kleinprojekte Integration; Projektförderung; Kleinprojekte; Förderbeitrag; Eingabetermin; gemeinnützige Organisationen; Migrationsgeschichte; Budget
Questions: Can my association get money from the Canton of Zurich for an integration project?; Wie kann ich ein Gesuch für ein Integrationsprojekt im Kanton Zürich einreichen?
Published facts:
Under the cantonal integration programme KIP 3 the Canton of Zurich has up to 300,000 francs a year available in 2024 to 2027 for projects that concern people with a migration history and/or are (co-)developed by them, particularly when they also involve migrants who can take part less well in social life, for example for language or financial reasons. The Fachstelle Integration states that it will also support projects during the cantonal integration programme KIP 4 (2028-2032), with 31 October 2027 as the first deadline, and that projects addressed specifically to refugees have their own funding programme.
Small projects with total costs of up to 5,000 francs can be submitted to the Canton of Zurich on a rolling basis as long as funds are still available, and simplified rules for submission and reporting apply to them.
For projects with total costs above 5,000 francs, 31 October 2026 is the last possible deadline within KIP 3. The maximum contribution per application is 50,000 francs, the Fachstelle Integration examines such applications within two months, and only projects completed by the end of 2027 at the latest can still be funded.
The Canton of Zurich funds projects in two priority areas in 2024 to 2027: living together and participation, where projects are supported that promote encounters, the participation of migrants in public life and voluntary work in the field of migration; and dealing with diversity and protection from discrimination, where projects are supported that promote a constructive approach to social diversity and that develop and implement measures against discrimination and racism. Only projects that concentrate on one or both of these areas receive contributions.
Municipalities and public as well as private non-profit organisations with their seat or a regional branch in the Canton of Zurich, such as associations or foundations, can apply for a contribution to an integration project.
Applications are submitted online, and the Canton of Zurich asks applicants to read its project funding guidelines for KIP 3 (2024-2027) first. There are separate forms for small projects and for larger projects. Questions about submitting a project and about reporting go to the specialists of the Fachstelle Integration, and the canton recommends contacting it before a first application.
The application pages of the Canton of Zurich state what an application needs: for a small project up to 5,000 francs a budget on the template the page provides; for a project above 5,000 francs a budget on that mandatory template and a concept or project description, for which the canton's template or the applicant's own may be used. Both pages warn that the web form cannot be saved in between, so all information and documents should be at hand.
The Fachstelle Integration names one specialist per funding area for questions about submitting a project and about reporting; on the access date of the page these were Maria Gstöhl, maria.gstoehl@ji.zh.ch, +41 43 259 25 30, for the area "living together and participation", and Deniz Yüksel, deniz.yueksel@ji.zh.ch, +41 43 259 25 27, for the area "dealing with diversity and protection from discrimination".

Label: The value-free limit for travellers bringing goods into Switzerland
Description: The total value up to which a traveller may bring goods into Switzerland free of value-added tax, how it counts per person and per day, and what happens above it. [FOCBS]
Aliases: Einkaeufe versteuern; how much can I bring into Switzerland tax free; value free limit customs Switzerland; 150 franc customs limit; do we get two allowances if we travel together; shopping abroad and bringing it back to Switzerland; customs allowance per person; Wertfreigrenze; wie viel darf ich zollfrei in die Schweiz einfuehren; Einkauf im Ausland Mehrwertsteuer Schweiz; Freigrenze 150 Franken; Wertfreigrenze mehrere Personen; mehrwertsteuerfrei; privaten Gebrauch; pro Person und pro Tag; Gesamtwert; Einzelne Gegenstände; MWST-pflichtig; Kurierdienst
Questions: We bought one item together while shopping abroad; do two of us get two allowances before we have to pay tax at the Swiss border?; Wie viel darf ich bei der Einreise in die Schweiz einkaufen, bevor ich Mehrwertsteuer bezahlen muss?
Published facts:
A traveller entering or returning to Switzerland may bring in goods up to a total value of CHF 150 free of value-added tax, provided the goods are for their private use or intended as gifts.
The value-free limit can be claimed only once per person and per day, and it applies to children as well.
Goods that are not for the traveller's private use and not intended as gifts are subject to value-added tax, and the value-free limit is not granted for them.
What counts towards the value-free limit is the value after deduction of the foreign value-added tax, where that tax is shown separately on the receipt or invoice.
If the total value of the goods brought in exceeds CHF 150, value-added tax is payable on the total value of the imported goods, not only on the amount above the limit.
A single item worth more than CHF 150 is always subject to value-added tax, irrespective of how many people are travelling together.
Different provisions apply to goods a traveller orders abroad, for example on the internet, and has delivered by post or courier service.
The value-free limit for value-added tax on entering Switzerland was reduced from CHF 300 to CHF 150 with effect from 1 January 2025.
A traveller bringing goods bought abroad into Switzerland often has the possibility of having the foreign value-added tax on them refunded.

Label: Which goods count towards the value-free limit
Description: What a traveller carries that is counted when the value-free limit is worked out, what is left out of it, and that the duty-free quantities are a second limit on top. [FOCBS]
Aliases: Reparatur am Auto im Ausland; what counts towards the customs limit; does my own luggage count at the Swiss border; do repairs abroad count towards the limit; is petrol counted at Swiss customs; was zaehlt zur Wertfreigrenze; Reiseproviant Zoll Schweiz; Autoreparatur im Ausland Zoll; Haustiere Wertfreigrenze; persoenliche Gebrauchsgegenstaende Grenze; Unterhaltsarbeiten; mitgeführten Waren; Reiseproviant; Treibstoff; Freimengen; Tabakfabrikate; Haustiere
Questions: Does the repair I had done on my car abroad count towards the value limit when I drive back into Switzerland?; Zaehlt der Treibstoff in meinem Tank zur Wertfreigrenze, wenn ich in die Schweiz einreise?
Published facts:
In principle all goods a traveller carries count towards the value-free limit, including duty-free food, tobacco products, alcoholic drinks, pets, and repair and maintenance work carried out abroad on the traveller's own vehicle.
The value of personal effects, of the traveller's own travel provisions and of the fuel in their vehicle is not counted towards the value-free limit.
On top of value-added tax, customs duty is payable when the goods a traveller carries exceed the duty-free quantities for alcoholic drinks, tobacco products and certain foodstuffs.

Label: The rate of value-added tax on goods brought into Switzerland
Description: The rate charged on imports once the value-free limit is passed, the reduced rate, and what the tax is calculated on. [FOCBS]
Aliases: Steuersatz Einfuhr; Prozent Einfuhrsteuer; how much VAT do I pay at the Swiss border; Swiss import VAT rate; reduced VAT rate on food at the border; what is the tax calculated on; Mehrwertsteuersatz Einfuhr Schweiz; wie viel Prozent Mehrwertsteuer Grenze; reduzierter Steuersatz Lebensmittel; Bemessung Mehrwertsteuer Einfuhr; Mehrwertsteuer beträgt; reduzierter Steuersatz; Marktwert; Quittung
Questions: Once I am over the limit, what rate of value-added tax do I pay at the Swiss border and what is it calculated on?; Wie hoch ist der Mehrwertsteuersatz bei der Einfuhr, und wovon wird er berechnet?
Published facts:
Value-added tax on goods brought into Switzerland is 8.1 per cent, with a reduced rate of 2.6 per cent for certain goods such as food, non-alcoholic drinks, books, magazines and medicines.
The tax is calculated on what the traveller paid for the goods, taken from the invoice, the receipt or the purchase contract; otherwise the market value is taxed, for example for gifts, meaning what a third party would have to pay for the item.
The import tax is levied on all imported goods, whatever the consignment is worth, and therefore also on consignments sent free of charge.
The reduced rate applies in particular to the import of foodstuffs other than alcoholic drinks, livestock, poultry and fish, cereals, seeds, planting stock and bulbs, live plants, cuttings and grafts, cut flowers and branches including those arranged into bouquets and wreaths, animal feed, silage acids and animal bedding, fertilisers, plant protection products, mulch and other plant-based ground cover, medicines, newspapers, magazines, books and other printed matter without advertising character, and products for monthly hygiene.

Label: Duty-free quantities for food, alcohol and tobacco
Description: The rule behind the duty-free quantities a traveller may bring in, how they are counted, and the restrictions on animal products; the quantities themselves are published as a graphic and are not served. [FOCBS]
Aliases: how much meat can I bring into Switzerland; duty free quantities Switzerland; bringing wine across the Swiss border; can I bring sausage from Italy; Freimengen Schweiz; wie viel Fleisch darf ich einfuehren; Alkohol ueber die Grenze Schweiz; Tierprodukte Einfuhr Schweiz; Freimenge Tabak; Freimengen; sensible Waren; Bruttogewicht; Tierprodukten; Reiseproviant; zollfrei
Questions: How much food and alcohol can I bring into Switzerland before customs duty is charged?; Welche Regeln gelten fuer Fleisch und Alkohol, die ich ueber die Grenze in die Schweiz bringe?
Published facts:
Goods a traveller brings in for their private use or as gifts are free of customs duty, except for so-called sensitive goods, on which duty is payable above a certain quantity for agricultural or health-policy reasons.
The duty-free quantities count per person and per day.
The gross weight is the basis on which the duty-free quantities are calculated.
Animal products may be brought into Switzerland only from EU member states, Iceland, Northern Ireland and Norway; bringing animal products in from other countries is prohibited.
Once the total value of the goods carried, including the value of all food, passes CHF 150, value-added tax is payable in any case.
Additional restrictions apply to certain animal products and to certain plant products, beyond the duty-free quantities.
Personal travel provisions, meaning ready-to-eat food and non-alcoholic drinks for the day of travel, may be brought in free of charge.
Bringing meat and dairy products, and most fruit and vegetables, from third countries, meaning non-EU states, is prohibited.

Label: Personal effects carried across the border
Description: The personal items a traveller may take out of and bring into Switzerland free of charge, and what counts as one. [FOCBS]
Aliases: do I pay customs on my own laptop; bringing my camera into Switzerland; personal belongings at the Swiss border; persoenliche Gebrauchsgegenstaende Zoll; Laptop Handy ueber die Grenze Schweiz; eigene Sachen zollfrei Schweiz; Sportgeraete Zoll Einreise; Sportgeräte; Mobiltelefone; Persönliche Gebrauchsgegenstände; abgabenfrei; Toilettenartikel; tragbare Computer
Questions: Do I have to declare my own laptop, phone and camera when I travel into Switzerland?; Muss ich meine eigene Kamera und meinen Laptop bei der Einreise in die Schweiz verzollen?
Published facts:
Personal effects may be brought into Switzerland free of charge.
Personal effects include the items a person resident in Switzerland took with them when they left the country.
Personal effects also include the items a person resident abroad uses during their stay in Switzerland and takes out again.
Clothes, laundry, toiletries, sports equipment, photo, film and video cameras, mobile telephones, portable computers and musical instruments are named as personal effects.

Label: Goods that may not be brought into Switzerland, or only under conditions
Description: That some goods are prohibited on import or restricted, with the examples the customs authority names. [FOCBS]
Aliases: nur mit Bewilligung einfuehren; what can I not bring into Switzerland; banned goods Swiss border; is it illegal to bring this into Switzerland; Einfuhrverbot Schweiz; verbotene Waren Zoll Schweiz; Faelschungen Zoll; Waffen Feuerwerk Einfuhr Schweiz; Bargeld Grenze Schweiz; Elefantenleder; Verbote und Beschränkungen; artengeschützte; Fälschungen; Feuerwerk
Questions: Are there things I am not allowed to bring into Switzerland at all?; Welche Waren darf ich nicht in die Schweiz einfuehren?
Published facts:
Certain goods may not be brought into Switzerland or are subject to restrictions, among them certain protected plants, animals and goods made from them, counterfeits, weapons, fireworks, medicines and cash.
Many souvenirs do not show that they are made from protected animals or plants, such as tropical wood, and much of it may not be brought into Switzerland at all or only with permits, so it is worth clarifying before the holiday which souvenirs are suitable and which are better left at the holiday destination.

Label: Declaring goods at the Swiss border
Description: How a traveller declares what they carry: unprompted at the crossing, with the QuickZoll app before it, through the green or the red channel, or with the green visual declaration in the car, and what entering the green channel commits them to. [FOCBS]
Aliases: Zoll am Flughafen; welcher Weg am Zoll; how do I declare goods at the Swiss border; red or green channel customs; nothing to declare Switzerland; declaring purchases at customs; QuickZoll app; Zollanmeldung Schweiz; gruener oder roter Durchgang; nichts zu verzollen; Sichtzollanmeldung Auto; Waren anmelden Grenze; Zollpersonal; unaufgefordert anmelden; QuickZoll; grünen Durchgang; roten Durchgang; verbindliche Zollanmeldung; strafbar; Sichtzollanmeldung; Armaturenbrett
Questions: I have something to declare at the airport - which channel do I take, and can I declare it before I land?; Wie melde ich Waren bei der Einreise in die Schweiz an, und was bedeutet der gruene Durchgang?
Published facts:
A traveller contributes to a swift customs assessment by having recognised and valid travel documents ready and by declaring, without being asked, all the goods and animals they are carrying.
For most goods the declaration can be made with the FOCBS QuickZoll app, which can also work out the cost of importing goods carried while travelling in advance; that calculation does not apply to internet shopping.
A traveller with nothing to declare can take the green route, for example at airports, and the FOCBS recommends the red channel to anyone unsure whether their goods have to be declared.
A traveller crossing the border by car can place the green visual customs declaration on the dashboard.
With the green visual declaration a traveller states that they and their fellow travellers carry recognised and valid travel documents and only goods that are free of charge within the duty-free quantities and the value-free limit or that they have cleared with the QuickZoll app; the green visual declaration is binding and customs staff may carry out checks without questioning the traveller.
At airports a traveller declares goods by choosing either the red or the green channel.
The green channel may be used only for goods that are free of charge within the duty-free quantities or the value-free limit of CHF 150, or that have been cleared with the QuickZoll app.
In both cases the goods taken through the green channel must not be subject to restrictions or prohibitions and must require neither a certificate nor a permit.
Entering the green channel counts as a binding customs declaration; a declaration can no longer be made up during a check by customs staff, and a traveller who takes the green channel while carrying prohibited goods, goods requiring a permit or dutiable goods is liable to prosecution.
A traveller carrying dutiable goods or goods subject to restrictions takes the red channel, where staff also answer any questions; the FOCBS also directs anyone unsure whether goods must be declared to the red channel.
QuickZoll works around the clock and everywhere, and no prior registration is needed to use it.
When paying the import charges in QuickZoll the traveller chooses a two-hour window in which they will cross the border, and the goods may then be brought in over any border crossing.
A traveller who does not want to split the goods by tax rate can declare all of them at the standard rate in QuickZoll, accepting that the standard rate is then applied to goods that would fall under the reduced rate as well.
Certain goods are subject to restrictions, permits or prohibitions and cannot be declared with QuickZoll, in particular vehicles, weapons and live animals; they must be declared at a border crossing staffed by FOCBS personnel.
On entering Switzerland a traveller must declare, without being asked, not only all the goods and animals they carry but also repair and maintenance work carried out on the vehicle.
Incorrect declarations and declarations that were not made count as punishable offences, and they can be penalised afterwards as well.
At border crossings where a written self-declaration is possible, the customs authority has set up a declaration box.
Entering Switzerland by train, a traveller can clear goods with the QuickZoll app, or declare them orally to customs staff present or in writing at a declaration box, and certain goods can be declared only at staffed border crossings.

Label: Ordering from abroad by post or courier
Description: What falls due on a consignment ordered abroad and delivered to Switzerland, who carries out the clearance, what the carrier charges on top, and the value up to which a gift between private persons is free of charge. [FOCBS]
Aliases: do I pay customs on a parcel from abroad; ordering online from Germany to Switzerland; what will my parcel cost at the border; customs clearance fee on a parcel; gift parcel from abroad Switzerland; Paket aus dem Ausland Zoll; Interneteinkauf Zoll Schweiz; Verzollungskosten Paket; Geschenksendung Schweiz zollfrei; online bestellt Mehrwertsteuer Schweiz; Warenwert; zoll- und mehrwertsteuerpflichtig; Transporteur; Verzollungskosten; Geschenksendungen; abgabenfrei; Tabakfabrikate; Paket-/Sendungsnummer; Postverzollungsprozess; Bruttogewicht; Zollinhaltserklärung
Questions: I ordered something online from a shop abroad; what will I have to pay when the parcel arrives in Switzerland?; Was muss ich bezahlen, wenn ich im Ausland online bestelle und das Paket in die Schweiz geliefert wird?
Published facts:
Every consignment from abroad is in principle subject to customs duty and value-added tax, and in postal and courier traffic the clearance is carried out by the carrier, such as DHL, UPS or Swiss Post.
The carrier charges clearance costs for its own work, and questions about those costs go to the carrier rather than to the customs authority.
Only the carrier can help trace a consignment, so the recipient should ask the sender for the parcel or consignment number and then approach that carrier.
A definitive calculation of what a consignment will cost is not possible in advance, because the carriers' own costs are not known to the customs authority beforehand; those costs are as a rule invoiced to the recipient together with the customs duties and taxes, and are to be clarified with the transport company.
Gift consignments from private persons abroad to private persons in Switzerland are free of charge up to a goods value of CHF 100, with the exception of tobacco products and alcoholic drinks.
For a gift consignment to be free of charge the sender must put a corresponding note on the outside of the parcel or letter.
A tracking status such as "held by customs" as a rule does not mean the parcel has been seized but that it is in the postal clearance process, which the post or the courier firm carries out and the customs authority does not, so the current status has to be asked of the courier firm or the post.
Customs duties are as a rule assessed on the gross weight including the packaging and often come to less than one Swiss franc per kilogram; alcoholic drinks, tobacco goods and food in particular carry higher customs duties or other high charges, such as beer tax or spirits tax.
For reasons of administrative economy, customs duties of up to five Swiss francs are not levied.
For reasons of administrative economy, tax amounts of up to five Swiss francs are not levied either, which corresponds to a taxable base of 62 Swiss francs at the 8.1 per cent rate or 193 Swiss francs at the 2.6 per cent rate.
Goods bought at an internet auction are treated under the general rules and not as a gift consignment.
The customs authority cannot refund foreign value-added tax; enquiries about reclaiming it go to the foreign customs authority or are to be settled through the foreign supplier.
The courier firms and the post charge various fees for their services in the customs assessment, often called clearance costs; the fees differ from firm to firm and the customs authority has no influence over them.
For a parcel sent by post the sender fills in the CN 23 customs content declaration and encloses a copy of the invoice or another proof of value, and for a letter sent by post the sender sticks a completed green CN 22 label on the envelope, where a copy of the invoice is enough as the statement of value.

Label: Mail-order and platform taxation, and why a shop charges Swiss VAT at checkout
Description: When a mail-order company or a platform operator has to register for Swiss value-added tax, and what changes once it is registered - the tax is charged on the sale instead of at the border. [FOCBS]
Aliases: why did the online shop charge me Swiss VAT; foreign shop registered for Swiss VAT; platform taxation Switzerland; small consignment VAT rule; Versandhandelsregelung; Plattformbesteuerung; Kleinsendungen Mehrwertsteuer; auslaendischer Onlineshop Schweizer MWST; warum zahle ich MWST im Shop statt an der Grenze; Versandhandelsunternehmen; Plattformbetreiber; Kleinsendungen; Einfuhrsteuerbetrag; MWST-Register; Inlandsteuer
Questions: Why does a foreign online shop charge me Swiss value-added tax at checkout instead of my paying it when the parcel arrives?; Wann muss ein auslaendischer Onlineshop die Schweizer Mehrwertsteuer selbst abrechnen?
Published facts:
Because value-added tax is due on even the smallest turnover of a taxable business inside Switzerland while on import it is levied only from a tax amount of more than CHF 5, the legislator introduced the mail-order rule on 1 January 2019 and, in addition, platform taxation on 1 January 2025.
The mail-order rule makes mail-order companies that send small consignments, with an import tax amount of up to CHF 5, from abroad into Switzerland liable to the tax, and platform taxation does the same for platform operators, once they reach a turnover of at least CHF 100,000 from such deliveries.
Once a Swiss or foreign mail-order company, or the platform operator where the delivery is made through a platform, is entered in the Swiss value-added tax register, not only its deliveries inside Switzerland but also those from abroad into Switzerland are subject to the domestic tax.

Label: Reduced duty for goods originating in an agreement or developing country
Description: That goods originating in a free-trade-agreement state or a developing country can come in duty-free or at a reduced rate, and the value up to which a private, non-commercial consignment gets that preference without a proof of origin. [FOCBS]
Aliases: reduced customs duty free trade agreement; do I need a proof of origin for a parcel; tariff preference private parcel; goods originating in a developing country customs; Zollpraeferenz Ursprungswaren; Freihandelsabkommen Zoll Schweiz; Ursprungsnachweis noetig; Sendung privat an privat Zollpraeferenz; Entwicklungsländern; Ursprungswaren; Freihandelsabkommen; Zollpräferenz; Ursprungsnachweis; ohne kommerziellen Charakter
Questions: A friend is sending me something from a country with a free trade agreement; do they have to include a proof of origin for the reduced customs duty?; Brauche ich fuer eine private Sendung einen Ursprungsnachweis, damit die Zollpraeferenz gilt?
Published facts:
Goods originating in states with which a free trade agreement exists, or in developing countries, can mostly be imported free of duty or at reduced rates, which is called tariff preference.
For consignments from one private person to another without commercial character, up to a value of as a rule 900 Swiss francs under a free trade agreement or 500 Swiss francs for developing countries, the tariff preference for originating goods can be granted without a proof of origin.

Label: Bringing a vehicle when moving to Switzerland
Description: How the customs side of a move with a road vehicle, a boat or an aircraft works - when the vehicle has to be cleared, what to do when that was missed, the permit for using it uncleared, and the proof of clearance each authority wants. [FOCBS]
Aliases: Auto an der Grenze; do I have to clear my car through customs when I move to Switzerland; bringing my car when I relocate; I forgot to clear my car at the border; driving a foreign car in Switzerland after moving; bringing a boat when moving to Switzerland; Auto verzollen Umzug Schweiz; Fahrzeug Uebersiedlungsgut Zoll; Zollbewilligung Fahrzeug unverzollt; Verzollungsnachweis Strassenverkehrsamt; Abfertigungszeiten; zollamtliche Abfertigung; besetzten Dienststellen; Zollbewilligung 15.30; Verzollungsnachweis; kantonalen Strassenverkehrsamt; kantonalen Schifffahrtsamt
Questions: We are moving to Switzerland with our car; does it have to be cleared through customs, and what happens if we drive across without doing it?; Muss ich mein Auto beim Umzug in die Schweiz verzollen, und was mache ich, wenn ich das verpasst habe?
Published facts:
The general provisions for removal goods apply to road vehicles, water craft and aircraft alike.
The customs clearance of a personal vehicle after a change of residence must take place at the vehicle's first crossing into Switzerland, at a staffed customs office that handles removal goods.
A traveller who missed that clearance must make it up at once at a staffed customs office, within the clearance hours for commercial goods; the vehicle has to be there, no appointment is needed, and form 18.44 with the evidence it lists is required.
Where the conditions for assessment as removal goods are not met, a customs permit 15.30 can be applied for under certain conditions, which allows the vehicle to be used uncleared for at most two years from the change of residence, and Swiss control plates must be applied for after one year at the latest.
For admission at the cantonal road traffic office the customs office issues an inspection report on form 13.20 A as proof of clearance, and questions about vehicle registration are for that cantonal office.
For a water craft the customs office issues proof of clearance on form 15.10 for admission at the cantonal shipping office, and questions about registration are for that office.
For an aircraft the customs office issues proof of clearance on form 15.15 for the Federal Office of Civil Aviation.
Where the vehicle was used abroad for less than six months, it may be used in Switzerland uncleared under a customs permit on form 15.30 for at most two years from the first day of entry, and after that period it must either be cleared, with customs duty, automobile tax and value-added tax, or be exported again.

Label: Moving to Switzerland with pets or horses
Description: What the customs authority asks for beyond the removal-goods rules when a move brings pets or horses along, and which office publishes the veterinary conditions. [FOCBS]
Aliases: Pferd Papiere Umzug; moving to Switzerland with a dog; bringing my cat when I relocate; moving with a horse to Switzerland; what do I need at the border for my pet; Umzug mit Haustieren Schweiz; Pferd Umzug Schweiz Zoll; Equidenpass Einfuhr; Haustier Grenze Schweiz Dokumente; Heimtiere; Equidenpass; Einfuhrzeugnis; tiergerecht
Questions: We are moving to Switzerland with our dog and our horse; what does customs want at the border?; Was muss ich beim Umzug in die Schweiz fuer mein Haustier oder mein Pferd vorlegen?
Published facts:
For pets such as dogs and cats the customs authority points to the additional provisions of the Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office on travelling to Switzerland with pets.
For horses from countries of the EU and from Norway an equine passport and an import certificate are submitted with the removal papers.
The transport of the animal, whether by car, by aircraft or by rail, must be done in a way appropriate to the animal, and the provisions of the Animal Welfare Act and of IATA are to be observed without fail.
Animals brought as removal goods follow the same rules on exemption from charges as the other belongings and are listed on the inventory as well, and the veterinary provisions have to be observed on top of that.

Label: Sending an item back, and repairs
Description: What to note when an item comes back to Switzerland or goes abroad as a return or for repair, and how a refund of import charges is applied for. [FOCBS]
Aliases: Abgaben zurueck; Ware zuruecksenden; sending an online purchase back abroad; getting import duty back after a return; repair abroad and bring it back; I refused the parcel can I get the tax back; Ruecksendung Zoll Schweiz; Rueckerstattung Einfuhrabgaben; Reparatur Ausland Zoll; Annahmeverweigerung Paket Zoll; Wiederausfuhr; Rücksendung; Veranlagungsverfügung; Rückerstattung von Einfuhrabgaben; Kreisdirektion; Veredelung
Questions: I sent back a jacket I had paid duty and tax on; how do I get that money back, and by when?; Wie bekomme ich die Einfuhrabgaben zurueck, wenn ich eine Sendung zurueckschicke?
Published facts:
A request for the refund of import charges is sent to the district directorate named on the assessment decision, and the time limit of 60 days from the issue of that decision must be kept, because requests submitted late are rejected.
So that a consignment returned to Switzerland arrives without trouble, the sender notes in the accompanying document, for example the delivery note, that it is a return, such as a refusal to accept.
For an item repaired in Switzerland and sent back abroad, the sender notes in the accompanying document that it is a repair or a warranty repair, and asks the foreign post or courier firm about the dispatch rules.
Where a Swiss manufacturer does more than repair an item, for example fitting a faster motor to a machine or chroming a surface, the provisions on processing traffic apply, which the customs authority publishes under its information for companies.
The mere fact that an imported item is exported again gives no entitlement to a refund of the import charges; further conditions have to be met before they can be refunded.
One of the cases the customs authority distinguishes is a re-export because the buyer has withdrawn from the purchase contract in agreement with the foreign supplier, for example because the goods are not liked, do not fit, are not of the quality wanted or are not what was ordered.
For such goods, imported personally for private use and exported again personally within six months, a request for a refund can be made orally or in writing at a service office.
To deal with that request the service office needs the original assessment decision, for example the customs cash receipt, and a confirmation from the foreign shop, as a receipt or an invoice, showing that the amount paid was refunded or credited.
For goods exported again after six months, goods not imported personally, such as mail order, or goods not exported again personally, such as a return by post, the customs authority sets out the procedure in its publication on the refund of import charges because of re-export.
When goods are exported for repair no charges are refunded on export; on their re-import only the repair costs have to be taxed, if it can be shown that the goods were exported beforehand for the repair.
Where a free replacement item is imported instead of the repaired one, under a warranty claim or as a goodwill gesture, the import tax is levied at the time of import but there is an entitlement to a refund.

Label: Bringing a pet into Switzerland, and buying a dog abroad
Description: What customs asks when a pet crosses the border - the crossing and the hours, the charges on an animal bought abroad, what to do when the declaration was missed, and the ban on dogs with cropped ears with its two exceptions. [FOCBS]
Aliases: Welpe aus dem Ausland; Hund beim Zuechter kaufen; bringing a dog into Switzerland; I bought a puppy abroad what do I do at the border; do I pay tax on a dog bought abroad; cropped ear dog Switzerland; I forgot to declare my dog at the border; Hund im Ausland gekauft Zoll; Heimtier einfuehren Schweiz; kupierte Hunde Einfuhrverbot; nachtraegliche Anmeldung Heimtier; Mehrwertsteuer Hund Einfuhr; Veranlagungszeiten; besetzten Grenzübergang; Veranlagungszeiten im Reiseverkehr; Kompetenzzentrum Heimtiere; zollfrei; kupierte Hunde
Questions: I bought a dog abroad and am driving it home to Switzerland; where do I have to cross, and what will I pay?; Was muss ich am Zoll tun, wenn ich einen im Ausland gekauften Hund in die Schweiz bringe?
Published facts:
The import of pets must go over a staffed border crossing and during the assessment hours for travel traffic, and the animal has to be presented in person to the control officers together with the forms the import requires.
Animals bought abroad and imported into Switzerland are free of customs duty, but value-added tax of 8.1 per cent of the value of the goods is payable, and showing a receipt makes the customs assessment easier.
Requests for a retroactive assessment of pets go without exception to the Pet Competence Centre of the customs authority, on its notification form and with the documents point 4 of that form lists.
A retroactive declaration always brings additional costs, and the opening of criminal proceedings remains reserved.
The import of dogs with cropped ears is prohibited, and such dogs are turned back at the border.
Owners resident abroad may bring their cropped dog to Switzerland for a holiday or another short stay, declaring the dog to customs on entry and providing a security.
A person moving from abroad to Switzerland may also import their cropped dog, but only if the conditions for the duty-free import of removal goods are met.
The provisions of the country the animal comes from are to be clarified directly in that country, with its embassy or with the foreign customs office.

Label: Leaving Switzerland with goods, and the Swiss VAT refund for a buyer resident abroad
Description: That a person leaving with their own private goods has no special customs rules to follow, and what a buyer resident abroad has to do to get the Swiss value-added tax on a purchase back. [FOCBS]
Aliases: Steuer bei der Ausreise; Rueckerstattung fuer Besucher; get the Swiss VAT back on something I bought here; tax free shopping Switzerland tourist; export document stamped at the border; taking my own things out of Switzerland; steuerfrei einkaufen Schweiz; Mehrwertsteuer zurueck Tourist; Ausfuhrdokument im Reiseverkehr; Ausreise Schweiz Zoll Privatwaren; keine besonderen Zollvorschriften; Ausfuhrzölle; Mindesteinkaufwert; Steuerbefreiung; besetzte Grenz-Zollstelle; Abfertigungszeiten
Questions: A visitor bought a watch in Switzerland and is flying home; how does she get the Swiss value-added tax back?; Wie bekomme ich als im Ausland wohnhafte Kundin die Schweizer Mehrwertsteuer auf meinem Einkauf zurueck?
Published facts:
On leaving Switzerland with private goods there are in principle no special customs rules to observe and no export duties to pay, but possible prohibitions, permits and restrictions should be clarified with the responsible authorities before departure.
The seller explains how and under what conditions tax-free shopping in Switzerland is possible; the minimum purchase value per sales transaction is 300 Swiss francs including value-added tax, and there is no tax exemption for smaller purchases.
So that the export can be confirmed, the buyer must leave Switzerland over a staffed border customs office, declare the goods orally at the moment of crossing and present the export document for travel traffic.
The confirmation of export on the export document is only given within the clearance hours of the border crossings; outside those hours or at unstaffed crossings no export can be confirmed.
Export confirmations that were not given at the border can also be made afterwards by other offices, and the Federal Tax Administration gives further information on that.

Label: What an insured person pays themselves - franchise, retention and hospital contribution
Description: The share of the costs an insured person resident in Switzerland pays themselves, the franchise and the optional higher ones, the retention and its annual cap, the daily hospital contribution, what is exempt, and how a change of franchise or of insurer works. [FOPH]
Aliases: what do I pay myself at the doctor in Switzerland; health insurance deductible Switzerland; franchise and retention explained; how much is the excess on Swiss health insurance; can I change my franchise; Franchise Krankenkasse; Selbstbehalt Krankenversicherung; Kostenbeteiligung; Wahlfranchise aendern; Spitalbeitrag pro Tag; was bezahle ich selber beim Arzt; Selbst-Behalt; Franchise aufgebraucht; Spitalbeitrag; zweimal die Franchise bei einem Wechsel; Behandlungsdatum massgebend; what happens when my franchise is used up; do I pay the deductible twice if I switch mid-year; is there a yearly maximum I pay myself; Ordentliche Franchise; Selbstbehalt; wählbare Franchise; Spitalaufenthaltes; Mutterschaftsleistungen; Wahlfranchisen; Kündigungsfrist; Spezialitätenliste; Wahl einer höheren Franchise; Beginn eines Kalenderjahres; Wechsel zu einer tieferen Franchise; wählbaren Franchisen
Questions: My child broke an arm and the bill is over a thousand francs; how much of that do we pay ourselves?; Wie viel muss ich bei einer Behandlung selbst bezahlen, und wie hoch ist die Franchise?
Published facts:
Insured persons take part in the costs of the services they use by paying a franchise, a retention and a contribution to the costs of hospital stays.
The ordinary franchise is 300 francs a year, children and adolescents pay none, and a higher franchise can be chosen voluntarily for insurance models with reduced premiums.
The retention is 10 per cent of the costs above the franchise, up to a maximum of 700 francs a year, and 350 francs a year for children and adolescents up to 18.
The contribution to the costs of a hospital stay is 15 francs a day without a time limit, and children and adolescents up to 18, young adults up to 25 in education and women for maternity services pay none.
Specific maternity services are exempt from cost sharing, namely the check-ups during and after the pregnancy including ultrasound examinations, the birth and birth assistance, birth-preparation courses and breastfeeding advice.
From the 13th week of pregnancy until eight weeks after the birth a woman no longer takes part in the costs of general medical services and nursing care in case of illness, including for an illness unconnected with the pregnancy.
Certain measures of medical prevention are also covered in full.
What decides which calendar year a treatment counts towards is the date of the treatment and not the date on which it is billed to the insurer.
For an adult with the ordinary annual franchise the franchise and the retention together come to at most 1,000 francs in a calendar year, and children up to 18 pay no franchise and at most 350 francs of retention.
Besides the ordinary franchise there are optional higher annual franchises of 500, 1,000, 1,500, 2,000 and 2,500 francs for adults and of 100, 200, 300, 400, 500 and 600 francs for children; an insurer does not have to offer every level and may offer different levels to young adults from 19 up to the completed age of 25.
Cost sharing applies to hospital treatment, outpatient and inpatient alike, in the same way as to other treatment, so long as the annual amount has not already been reached through other outpatient treatment.
Contributions to bathing cures and to the aids and articles on the list of means and articles are subject to the franchise and the retention as well, unless these have already been used up, so the insured person may get no contribution or only part of one and may receive a further contribution from a supplementary insurance.
The franchise and the retention are each owed only once in a calendar year even when the insured person changes insurer during the year, and a confirmation of the amount already used has to be obtained from the previous insurer.
The franchise is owed for each calendar year even when one course of treatment runs across the turn of the year, so in the worst case an insured person pays the cost sharing twice in succession.
An insured person can move from a higher optional franchise to a lower one or to the ordinary franchise from the start of the next calendar year whatever their state of health, if the notice period is kept, and the lower franchise must be communicated to the insurer in writing by 30 November; a higher franchise also takes effect at the start of a calendar year and should be notified in good time, at the latest by the middle of December.
On a change of insurer during the year it is not possible to move from the ordinary franchise to an optional higher one, which is possible only at the start of a calendar year.
A model with a restricted choice of provider can be combined with a higher annual franchise, subject to the insurer's rules on the maximum discount.
A bonus insurance may not be offered together with an optional higher franchise.
The insurer levies a retention of 40 per cent instead of 10 per cent when the insured person gets a medicine that can be exchanged for a comparable and clearly cheaper one on the list of specialities, and the retention stays at 10 per cent when the doctor expressly prescribes the original preparation for medical reasons.

Label: What makes premiums differ - the canton, the premium region and how they are paid
Description: Who sets the premium, what it may be graded by, how a canton is divided into premium regions and who decides which region a municipality falls into, and when the premium is due. The release does not publish premium amounts. [FOPH]
Aliases: why is my premium higher than my neighbour's; premium regions Switzerland; does my premium depend on where I live; who decides health insurance premiums; when do I pay my health insurance premium; Praemienregionen; kantonale Praemienunterschiede; warum unterscheiden sich die Krankenkassenpraemien; Praemie monatlich bezahlen; Praemie haengt vom Wohnort ab; drei verschiedene Regionaltarife; Praemie nach Altersgruppe; mittlere Praemie; Praemienrechner; Praemien sind unabhaengig vom Einkommen; why do I pay more than my colleague; premium by age group; Prämienregionen; maximal zulässigen Prämienunterschiede; unterschiedliche Prämien festlegen; Wohnsitzgemeinde des Versicherten; kantonalen Kostenunterschieden; regional abstufen; im Voraus; genehmigt und publiziert; zur Genehmigung einreichen; Kostendeckung; Gleichbehandlung der Kantone; Stellungnahme
Questions: A colleague two towns away pays less than I do for the same insurer; how can that be?; Wovon haengt die Hoehe meiner Krankenkassenpraemie ab, und wann muss ich sie bezahlen?
Published facts:
Where costs differ within a larger canton, the canton is divided into two or three premium regions, and the Federal Department of Home Affairs determines the maximum premium differences allowed between the regions.
In the cantons of Bern, Graubuenden, Lucerne, St Gallen and Zurich the municipalities are divided into three premium regions, and in the cantons of Basel-Landschaft, Fribourg, Schaffhausen, Ticino, Vaud and Valais there are two.
Health insurers may set different premiums for the premium regions, so in a canton with several regions the premium also depends on the municipality the insured person lives in and the region that municipality belongs to.
The premium regions that apply and the maximum discounts allowed between them are laid down in the ordinance of the Federal Department of Home Affairs on premium regions, SR 832.106.
The ordinance of the Federal Department of Home Affairs lays down which premium region each municipality falls into, and that ordinance is always the decisive source.
The insurer sets the amount of the premiums of its insured persons and, unless the law provides an exception, levies the same premium from all of them.
The insurer grades the premiums according to the differences in cost between cantons, and what decides is the place of residence of the insured person.
The insurer may grade the premiums by region in addition, and the Federal Department of Home Affairs sets those regions uniformly.
Premiums are paid in advance and as a rule monthly.
The health insurers calculate the premiums themselves, and the Federal Office of Public Health approves them and publishes them.
The insurers have to submit the premiums of the compulsory health insurance and of the voluntary individual daily allowance insurance to the Federal Office of Public Health as the supervisory authority for approval.
The Federal Office of Public Health approves only premiums that meet the legal requirements, that secure the insurer's solvency and protect the interests of the insured, and that cover the costs without lying unreasonably above them or leading to excessive reserves.
In examining the submitted premiums the Federal Office of Public Health checks in particular whether the expected premium income will cover the expected costs, and that cost coverage has to be kept for each insurer and each canton separately, so that the cantons are treated equally.
The cantons take part in the approval of the premiums - the Federal Office of Public Health asks them for their opinion on the forecast of the costs and sends them the insurers' first submission, and they may comment on the costs in their own area.

Label: Insurance models with a restricted choice of provider
Description: Models in which the insured person limits their choice of provider by agreement with the insurer, what the insured undertakes in return, and the categories the premium comparison uses from the 2027 premiums. [FOPH]
Aliases: family doctor model health insurance; HMO model Switzerland; telemedicine insurance model; is the cheaper model worth it; what do I give up with a restricted model; Hausarztmodell; HMO Modell Krankenkasse; Telmed Modell; eingeschraenkte Wahl der Leistungserbringer; Gruppenpraxis; HMO-Modell; Gesundheits-Telefon; zuerst zum Hausarzt gehen; guenstigeres Versicherungsmodell; Modell wechseln jederzeit; which insurance model should I choose; group practice insurance model; cheaper model with a first point of contact; eingeschränkte Wahl der Leistungserbringer; Prämien tiefer ausfallen; Anlaufstelle zu konsultieren; erste Anlaufstelle; PRAXIS; TEL_DIG; PHARM; FLEX; jederzeit möglich; Ende eines Kalenderjahres möglich
Questions: My insurer offers a cheaper family-doctor model; what do I give up if I take it?; Was bedeutet ein Versicherungsmodell mit eingeschraenkter Wahl der Leistungserbringer fuer mich?
Published facts:
Insurance models let insured persons limit their right to choose, by agreement with the insurer, to providers the insurer selects with a view to more economical care.
In return for the restricted choice of provider insurers may reduce the premiums for these models, so the premiums can be lower than for insurance without a restricted choice.
The insured undertake to consult first, whenever they have a health problem, the point of contact provided for in the model they chose, and the models may set requirements about the choice of particular providers or about the dispensing of medicines.
From the premiums for the year 2027 the new categories PRAXIS, PHARM, TEL_DIG and FLEX are introduced in the federal premium calculator.
The categories Hausarzt and HMO are brought together under the name PRAXIS, the category for other models, which mainly covered telephone models, is renamed TEL_DIG, and two new categories PHARM and FLEX are created.
In the models of the PRAXIS category the first point of contact for health questions is always a given medical practice, such as the family doctor or a medical centre, which refers the insured person to a specialist where needed.
In the TEL_DIG category the first contact happens by telephone or digitally, for example through a telemedicine centre or an app.
In the PHARM category the first point of contact for health questions is a partner pharmacy of the insurer.
In the FLEX category several first points of contact are available and the insured person can choose freely between them, for example between a medical practice and a telemedicine centre or between a telemedicine centre and a partner pharmacy.
Insurers offer different models, so before choosing one the insured person should read the insurance conditions and documents carefully and consider whether the model fits their situation.
Moving from an insurance without a restricted choice of provider into one with a restricted choice is possible at any time.
Moving out of a model with a restricted choice of provider to another form of insurance, or to another insurer, is possible only at the end of a calendar year and only keeping the notice periods that the health insurance act sets for the ordinary change of insurer, while a change of insurer during the calendar year on one of the special grounds the act provides stays open.

Label: Unpaid premiums, debt enforcement and the suspension of cover
Description: What the insurer does when premiums or cost sharing are not paid, what the canton takes over when a certificate of loss is issued, and the list that leads to a suspension of cover with emergency treatment excepted. [FOPH]
Aliases: I cannot pay my health insurance premium; what happens if I do not pay my premiums; can they cancel my health insurance; health insurance debt enforcement Switzerland; Praemien nicht bezahlt; Betreibung Krankenkasse; schwarze Liste Krankenkasse; Leistungsaufschub; Schulden bei der Krankenkasse; Mahnung der Krankenkasse; kein Wechsel bei offenen Schulden; saeumige versicherte Person; cannot switch insurer with unpaid premiums; Mahnung; Zahlungsaufforderung; Betreibungsverfahren; Verlustscheins; Notfallbehandlungen; Leistungskosten; säumige versicherte Person; den Versicherer nicht wechseln; Verzugszinse und Betreibungskosten
Questions: I have not paid my premiums for months; can my insurer stop paying my bills?; Was passiert, wenn ich meine Krankenkassenpraemien nicht bezahle?
Published facts:
When an insured person does not pay premiums or cost sharing that are due, the insurer sends a reminder, then a demand for payment, and finally opens debt enforcement proceedings against them.
The canton takes over 85 per cent of the claims that led to the issue of a certificate of loss or an equivalent legal title.
Cantons may put on a list insured persons who do not meet their duty to pay premiums despite debt enforcement, and on the canton's notification the insurers suspend the taking over of the costs of services for those insured persons, emergency treatment excepted.
As soon as the insured person settles the outstanding claims, the insurer tells the responsible cantonal authority that the suspension of cover is to end.
By way of exception to the ordinary right to change insurer, an insured person in arrears may not change insurer for as long as the outstanding premiums, cost sharing, default interest and debt enforcement costs are not paid in full; children may not change insurer while such arrears exist for them; and an insured person who has arrears only for their children may change insurer all the same.

Label: What basic insurance pays for, and who decides
Description: The scope of the benefits compulsory health insurance must cover, the test a benefit has to meet, that every insurer owes the same scope, how tariffs are set, and the dental exception. [FOPH]
Aliases: what does basic health insurance cover; does the Krankenkasse pay for dental treatment; are all insurers the same for basic insurance; who decides what is covered; Grundversicherung Leistungen; was zahlt die Krankenkasse; zahnaerztliche Behandlung Krankenkasse; wirksam zweckmaessig wirtschaftlich; was bezahlt die Grundversicherung; zahlt die Krankenkasse Physiotherapie; zahlt die Krankenkasse eine Operation; zahlt die Krankenkasse Medikamente; Spezialitaetenliste; does basic insurance pay for physiotherapy; is a hospital stay covered by basic insurance; Leistungen bei Krankheit; wirksam, zweckmässig und wirtschaftlich; gesetzlich vorgeschriebenen Leistungsumfang; zahnärztliche Behandlungen; schwere Allgemeinerkrankung; nicht vermeidbaren Erkrankungen des Kausystems; schweren Allgemeinerkrankungen; Krankheitswert
Questions: Does basic insurance pay for dental treatment, and does it cover the same things at every insurer?; Welche Leistungen uebernimmt die obligatorische Krankenpflegeversicherung?
Published facts:
Compulsory health insurance grants benefits in case of illness, accident and maternity, among them examinations and treatment by doctors and in hospital, nursing care and certain non-medical services, and in case of accident the health insurer steps in only where the insured person has no other cover.
Every insurer that carries out the compulsory health insurance must cover the same scope of benefits laid down by law and must treat insured persons equally, and may not pay further benefits beyond that scope.
By law the compulsory health insurance covers only benefits that are effective, appropriate and economical, and benefits that may not meet those criteria, new ones as well as existing ones, are examined in the Health Technology Assessment programme.
Where a provider carries out services that are not among the obligatory benefits of the compulsory health insurance, the provider must point that out to the patient.
Dental treatment is in principle not covered; only dental treatment made necessary by a serious and unavoidable disease of the masticatory system or by a serious general illness or its consequences, or needed to treat such an illness or its consequences, is paid for, and according to settled case law the list of illnesses that require dental treatment at the expense of the compulsory health insurance is exhaustive.

Aliases: do I need supplementary hospital insurance; free choice of hospital Switzerland; out of canton hospital costs; Zusatzversicherung freie Spitalwahl; Listenspital ausserkantonal; brauche ich eine Zusatzversicherung; Zusatzversicherung kuendigen; andere Kuendigungsfristen fuer Zusatzversicherungen; Gesundheitsfragen bei der Zusatzversicherung; Zusatzversicherung muss nicht gekuendigt werden; can the insurer refuse supplementary insurance; Zusatzversicherung; freie Spitalwahl; Listenspital; ausserkantonale Spitalbehandlung; aus medizinischen Gründen notwendig

Published facts:
A supplementary insurance for the free choice of hospital throughout Switzerland can still be needed, because the insurer and the canton of residence share the reimbursement only up to what the treatment would have cost in a listed hospital of that canton, and a higher tariff at the treating hospital outside the canton is borne by the insured person or their supplementary insurance.
The compulsory health insurance covers the full cost of hospital treatment outside the canton of residence in every case where that treatment is necessary for medical reasons, that is in an emergency or where no listed hospital of the canton of residence offers the treatment in question.
