Questions: My premium is going up again; by when do I have to give notice to change insurer?; Welche Kuendigungsfrist gilt, wenn ich meine Krankenkasse wechseln will?
Published facts:
An insured person may change insurer at the end of a calendar half-year, keeping a notice period of three months.
When the new premium is notified, the insured person may change insurer with one month's notice to the end of the month preceding the month from which the new premium applies, and the insurer must notify each insured person of the new premiums approved by the Federal Office of Public Health at least two months in advance.
Where an insured person has to leave an insurer because they move their place of residence or change job, the insurance relationship ends at the moment of the move or of starting with the new employer.
The insurance relationship with the previous insurer ends only once the new insurer has told it that the person is insured with it without interruption of cover, and a new insurer that fails to give that notice must compensate the insured person for the damage, in particular the difference in premium.
Where the previous insurer makes the change of insurer impossible, it must compensate the insured person for the damage that results, in particular the difference in premium.
The previous insurer may not force an insured person who changes insurer to cancel the supplementary insurances taken out with it as well.

Label: Health insurance for cross-border commuters
Description: Health insurance for cross-border commuters with permit G who live in a neighbouring EU or EFTA state or the United Kingdom and work in Switzerland - the place-of-work principle, the right of option to stay insured where they live, the three-month window for it, why a merely tacit choice does not count, the French form, and the family members. [FOPH]
Aliases: cross-border commuter health insurance; can I keep my German health insurance and work in Switzerland; right of option health insurance Switzerland; exemption from Swiss health insurance for commuters; permit G health insurance; stay insured in France while working in Switzerland; Krankenversicherung Grenzgaenger; Optionsrecht Krankenversicherung; Befreiung von der Versicherungspflicht Grenzgaenger; Ausweis G Krankenversicherung Wohnsitzstaat; Grenzgaengerin Krankenversicherung; Optionsrecht ausueben; Erwerbsortsprinzip; nichterwerbstätigen Familienangehörigen; Optionsrecht; Sondervereinbarungen getroffen; innerhalb von drei Monaten; Befreiung von der Versicherungspflicht; Behörde des Arbeitskantons; stillschweigende Ausübung des Optionsrechts; nicht rechtsgültig; formelles Gesuch um Befreiung; visieren lassen; Nichterwerbstätige Familienangehörige
Questions: I live in Germany and work in Switzerland - can I keep my German health insurance instead of taking a Swiss one?; Ich wohne in Frankreich und arbeite in der Schweiz - kann ich mich stattdessen in Frankreich krankenversichern?
Published facts:
Under the agreement on the free movement of persons with the EU, the EFTA convention and the new social security agreement with the United Kingdom the duty to insure follows the place-of-work principle, so every person working in Switzerland, and their non-working family members, must in principle take out health insurance in Switzerland.
Switzerland has made special agreements with the neighbouring states, among them Germany, France, Italy and Austria, under which people with the citizenship of an EU state who live there may insure themselves in their country of residence instead of Switzerland, which is called the right of option.
A person who does not want to be insured in Switzerland must file an application for exemption from the duty to insure with the competent authority of the canton they work in, within three months of the start of the employment relationship.
According to a Federal Supreme Court judgment of March 2015 a merely tacit exercise of the right of option is not legally valid, so a cross-border commuter who was insured abroad rather than in Switzerland and never filed a formal application for exemption can still insure themselves in Switzerland under the health insurance act, once the competent authority of the canton they work in confirms that the option has not yet been validly exercised; on that confirmation the Swiss insurer takes the person on.
For France the person must, within three months, fill in the form on the choice of the health insurance system and have it stamped by the French health insurance fund, the caisse primaire d'assurance-maladie, before it is returned to the competent authority of the canton they work in.
For France a person who is insured in Switzerland and keeps working there but moves to France and wants to be insured there must send a copy of the stamped form to their Swiss health insurer at once, so that the Swiss insurance ends.
For Italy the non-working family members of a cross-border commuter living there must, depending on the circumstances, be insured either in Switzerland or in Italy.

Label: What health insurance pays for treatment abroad
Description: What the compulsory health insurance of a person living in Switzerland pays when they are treated abroad - the emergency case and what counts as one, treatment that cannot be given in Switzerland, birth abroad, and the ceiling on what is reimbursed. [FOPH, KVV]
Aliases: what does my health insurance pay if I get sick abroad; emergency treatment abroad health insurance; is treatment on holiday covered; can I go abroad for an operation and have it paid; how much does the Krankenkasse pay abroad; Krankenversicherung Ausland; Behandlung im Ausland; Notfall im Ausland Krankenkasse; doppelter Betrag Ausland; Territorialitaetsprinzip; voruebergehender Auslandaufenthalt; am I covered on holiday abroad; Krank im Ausland; Leistungen im Ausland; im Ausland behandeln lassen; Kostenübernahme; wohnhafte und versicherte Personen; in Notfällen im Ausland; vorübergehenden Auslandsaufenthalt; Rückreise in die Schweiz nicht angemessen; doppelte Betrag
Questions: What does my health insurance pay if I fall ill on holiday abroad?; Was zahlt meine Krankenversicherung, wenn ich im Ausland krank werde?
Published facts:
A person who is resident in Switzerland and insured there can in certain cases be treated abroad at the expense of the compulsory health insurance.
The conditions under which the costs of treatment abroad are covered differ according to the country in which the treatment is given and according to the kind of treatment.
The compulsory health insurance covers the costs of treatment given abroad in an emergency, and an emergency exists where an insured person needs medical treatment during a temporary stay abroad and a return journey to Switzerland is not reasonable; there is no emergency where the insured person travels abroad for the purpose of that treatment.
The Federal Department of Home Affairs designates, after hearing the competent commission, the benefits whose costs the compulsory health insurance covers abroad because they cannot be provided in Switzerland.
The compulsory health insurance covers the costs of a birth that took place abroad where only in that way the child could acquire the citizenship of its mother or father, or where the child would be stateless if it were born in Switzerland.
For treatment abroad that cannot be given in Switzerland, for emergencies abroad and for treatment abroad of cross-border commuters, posted employees, people in the public service and their family members, at most twice the amount that would be reimbursed in Switzerland is covered, and for a birth abroad at most the single amount.

Label: Premiums, premium reduction and cost-sharing for insured people living abroad
Description: For people who live in an EU or EFTA state or the United Kingdom and remain compulsorily insured in Switzerland - which premium they pay, how the insurer sets it per country, who grants the premium reduction, and that they share the costs of their treatment. [FOPH]
Aliases: health insurance premium when living in the EU; Swiss health insurance while living abroad; premium reduction for pensioners living abroad; who pays my premium reduction if I live in France; cost sharing when I live abroad and am insured in Switzerland; Praemien Wohnsitz im Ausland; Praemienverbilligung im Ausland; Kostenbeteiligung im Ausland wohnhafte Versicherte; Schweizer Rente im Ausland Krankenkasse; Gemeinsame Einrichtung KVG; nichterwerbstaetige Familienangehoerige im Ausland; nur ein Drittel der Krankenkassen; Swiss pensioner living in the EU; Wohnsitzstaat geltenden Prämien; eigene Prämie zu berechnen; Kostenunterschiede zu berücksichtigen; bescheidenen wirtschaftlichen Verhältnissen; Kanton des Wohnortes; Kanton des Arbeitsortes; Kostenbeteiligung; im Ausland wohnhafte Versicherte; unterschiedlich geregelt
Questions: I live in an EU country and am still insured in Switzerland - which premium do I pay and can I get a premium reduction?; Ich wohne im Ausland und bin in der Schweiz krankenversichert - wer ist fuer meine Praemienverbilligung zustaendig?
Published facts:
People living in an EU or EFTA state or the United Kingdom who are subject to compulsory Swiss health insurance under the agreement on the free movement of persons, the EFTA convention or the new social security agreement with the United Kingdom have to pay the premiums that apply to their state of residence.
About a third of the Swiss health insurers offer insurance to people living in an EU or EFTA state or the United Kingdom, and some of them are active only in individual EU states.
The insurer has to calculate its own premium for each state and to take the cost differences between the states into account, so that the premiums cover the costs caused by the insured people living in each of those states.
Switzerland grants a premium reduction to people in modest economic circumstances who are insured under the compulsory health insurance and live in the EU, in EFTA or in the United Kingdom.
For the premium reduction of pensioners and their family members living in the EU, in EFTA or in the United Kingdom the Confederation is responsible, and it is carried out by the joint institution under the health insurance act.
For the premium reduction of people employed in Switzerland, of cross-border commuters, of people drawing unemployment insurance benefits and of their family members who live in the EU, in EFTA or in the United Kingdom the canton of residence is responsible, and for cross-border commuters the canton they work in.
Insured people living abroad have to share the costs of the medical treatment they receive in Switzerland and in some cases of the treatment they receive abroad.
How much an insured person living abroad shares in those costs is regulated differently depending on the country in which that person is insured.

Label: Who gets the bill and who pays it
Description: How a bill for treatment reaches the patient or the insurer - the two systems the act sets up, what a bill has to contain, that it comes electronically unless paper is asked for, and who may see the medical details. [KVG]
Aliases: who pays the doctor's bill; I got a bill from my doctor what do I do; do I pay the doctor and get the money back; does the hospital bill my insurer directly; Tiers garant; Tiers payant; Arztrechnung wer bezahlt; Rechnung an die Krankenkasse schicken; Rueckerstattung von der Krankenkasse; Kopie der Rechnung vom Spital; Rechnung in Papierform verlangen; System des Tiers garant; System des Tiers payant; Anspruch auf Rückerstattung; detaillierte und verständliche Rechnung; Kopie der Rechnung; in elektronischer Form; kostenlos in Papierform; Vertrauensarzt
Questions: My doctor sent the bill to me and not to my insurer - is that right, and what do I do with it?; Wer schuldet dem Arzt die Vergütung - ich oder meine Krankenkasse?
Published facts:
Unless the insurer and the provider have agreed otherwise, it is the insured person who owes the provider the payment for the treatment, and the insured person then has a claim for reimbursement against their insurer, which is the system known as tiers garant; that claim may be assigned to the provider.
The insurer and the provider may agree that the insurer owes the payment, which is the system known as tiers payant, and in the case of inpatient treatment the insurer owes the share of the payment that falls on it.
The provider has to send the debtor a detailed and comprehensible bill and to give them everything they need in order to check how the payment was calculated and whether the treatment was economical; under the tiers payant system the provider must send the insured person a copy of the bill without being asked.
The provider has to send the bills to the debtor electronically, and at the request of the insured person sends them on paper free of charge.
The provider is entitled in justified cases, and at the request of the insured person is obliged in every case, to disclose medical information only to the insurer's medical officer.
No form is needed in order to claim benefits from the compulsory health insurance.

Label: Suspending health insurance during military or civilian service
Description: When long service suspends the duty to hold compulsory health insurance, from which day, and what has to be told to the insurer in order to stop paying premiums. [KVG, KVV]
Aliases: do I pay health insurance during military service; suspend health insurance during service; Krankenkasse waehrend dem Militaerdienst; Versicherungspflicht sistieren Militaerdienst; Krankenkasse pausieren Zivildienst; Zivilschutz Krankenkasse Praemien; Militaerversicherung statt Krankenkasse; keine Praemien waehrend dem Dienst; Versicherungspflicht wird sistiert; 60 aufeinander folgenden Tagen; Militärversicherung; Sistierung der Versicherungspflicht; von der Prämienzahlung befreit; mindestens acht Wochen vor deren Beginn
Questions: I am doing several months of service - do I have to keep paying my health insurance premiums?; Kann ich meine Krankenkasse während eines langen Militärdienstes sistieren?
Published facts:
The duty to hold compulsory health insurance is suspended for people who are subject to the Federal Act on Military Insurance for more than 60 consecutive days.
The suspension of the duty to insure begins on the day on which the insured person becomes subject to the military insurance.
The insured person is freed from paying premiums from the start of being subject to the military insurance if they tell their insurer at least eight weeks before it begins, and if they miss that period the insurer stops charging a premium from the next date it can manage, at the latest eight weeks after being told.
Where premiums are paid in spite of the suspension, the insurer sets them against premiums that fall due later or pays them back.
The insurer has to report to the cantonal authorities responsible for the premium reduction the people whose duty to insure has been suspended, and to tell them how long the suspension actually lasted.

Label: Signing on with the RAV and registering for Job-Room
Description: When and where a person who has lost their job or is threatened with unemployment signs on with the regional employment centre for public employment placement, and that registering on the Job-Room platform is a further, separate step. Registering serves both to get support with the job search and to make the claim for unemployment benefit, and it should not be left until the last working day. [SECO]
Aliases: sign on with the RAV; register with the RAV; register as unemployed; RAV Anmeldung; sich beim RAV anmelden; fruehzeitig beim RAV anmelden; Anmeldung oeffentliche Arbeitsvermittlung; Job-Room registrieren; Job-Room Registrierung; frühzeitig beim RAV; Anmeldung beim RAV; öffentlichen Arbeitsvermittlung; letzten Arbeitstag; Job-Room; Stellenplattform
Questions: When do I have to register with the RAV after I have been given notice?; Wann muss ich mich nach der Kündigung beim RAV anmelden?
Published facts:
A person losing their job registers as early as possible with the RAV for public employment placement, in order both to receive support with the job search and to make their claim to unemployment benefit, and should not wait until the last working day to do so.
In addition to signing on with the RAV, the person registers for Job-Room, the largest job platform in Switzerland, where various eServices and functions are available to them.
Early registration with the RAV together with registration for Job-Room brings two advantages - at the first consultation the RAV personal adviser helps build a job-search strategy tailored to the person's situation, and once registered for Job-Room the person gets preferred access, under the job-registration duty, to job advertisements before they are published publicly.

Label: Duty to look for work, applications and proof of efforts
Description: The legal duty of a person losing their job to look for work, when that search has to start for each kind of contract or situation, what makes an application count, how the number of applications is fixed, and how proof of the efforts must be kept for the RAV. It also covers what happens to the entitlement when the efforts are insufficient or the person is at fault for the job loss. [SECO]
Aliases: job search obligations while unemployed; how many job applications do I have to make; when do I have to start looking for a new job; proof of job applications for the RAV; sanctions for not applying for jobs; Arbeitsbemuehungen nachweisen; wie viele Bewerbungen pro Monat; wann mit der Stellensuche beginnen; Nachweis der Stellensuche; alles Zumutbare zu unternehmen; Arbeitsbemühungen; Kündigungsschreiben; Befristete oder temporäre Arbeitsverträge; Mutterschaftsurlaub; Saisonangestellte; Motivationsschreiben; Spontanbewerbungen; Nachweise; AVIG
Questions: How many job applications do I have to send while I am unemployed?; Wie viele Arbeitsbemühungen muss ich pro Monat nachweisen?
Published facts:
A person facing job loss or threatened notice starts looking for work immediately, because the law requires them to undertake everything that can reasonably be expected of them to avoid unemployment.
If the job-search efforts made before registering with the regional employment centre are insufficient, the number of daily allowances is reduced, which can mean receiving no compensation for several weeks at the start of unemployment, in some circumstances even for more than a month.
Entitlement to unemployment benefit can also be suspended temporarily if the person resigns without another job in prospect, or is dismissed through their own fault.
The job search has to begin before unemployment actually starts, and under an open-ended employment contract it begins as soon as the person knows the contract will end, whether by oral notice, by receipt of the letter of termination or by their own resignation, for at most the last 3 months before the employment relationship ends.
Under a fixed-term or temporary employment contract the job search has to run during the last 3 months of the contract, or during the whole contract period if that is shorter than 3 months.
After military service, civilian service or a return from abroad, the job search has to cover the 3 months before the registration with the RAV.
After maternity leave the job search has to begin from the 15th week after the birth.
After completing post-compulsory education the job search has to begin once the examination results are known, provided the registration with the RAV follows afterwards, and otherwise from the date of that registration if the person registers earlier.
Seasonal employees have to start looking for work 3 months before the expected end of the season, and their efforts must also cover permanent positions.
The quality of applications is decisive, which means a carefully prepared application with an up-to-date CV and a personally worded covering letter, for a position that genuinely matches the person's competences and abilities.
The page sets no fixed number of applications - how many are required depends on the person's situation, among other things their occupation, training, age, geographical mobility and language skills, and on the rules of their canton, and the person is told to contact their RAV as soon as possible to agree together how many job-search efforts are reasonable in their case.
The person is expected to vary their approach rather than only answering job advertisements, using their personal network, sending speculative applications and telephoning companies.
The RAV checks the job-search efforts, so every piece of evidence has to be kept carefully, for example in a dossier.
The evidence kept should include e-mails and letters together with the replies received, a note of the date, the company and the person spoken to for telephone calls and network contacts, and a business card or a company stamp for visits made in person.
These proofs have to be presented later to the personal adviser at the RAV so that unemployment benefit is received without restrictions.
In the Canton of Zurich the duty to look for work starts before unemployment begins - as soon as a person receives or gives notice they must look for a new job and document their search efforts, and with a fixed-term contract they must start looking 3 months before it expires.
A person drawing unemployment insurance benefits in the Canton of Zurich must apply for jobs sufficiently and appropriately, and as a rule 10 to 12 job-search efforts a month are expected.
In the Canton of Zurich the form proving the personal job-search efforts must be filled in correctly and completely and submitted by the 5th day of the following month.
A jobseeker in the Canton of Zurich must expect a reduction of their daily allowances if they make too few job-search efforts, do not spread them over the whole month, apply for unsuitable jobs or in an unsuitable form, submit the proof form too late, or cannot produce the job advertisements, application letters and rejection letters.
A jobseeker in the Canton of Zurich must apply for a job assigned to them by the RAV and may not refuse a suitable job that is offered, and a breach can be sanctioned with up to 60 suspension days, meaning that for up to three months no daily allowances are paid.
After registering at their RAV a jobseeker in the Canton of Zurich receives an e-mail inviting them to make a self-assessment of their application skills, so that they can work through the relevant topics before the first counselling interview.

Label: Waiting days, number of daily allowances and how long they last
Description: How the unemployment insurance daily allowance works in time - the waiting days served before the first payment, the five daily allowances a week, what counts as insured earnings, the two-year frame period, and the limits that apply during illness, pregnancy or accident. The release carries the rules and never an amount of benefit. [SECO]
Aliases: waiting days unemployment benefit; how many daily allowances can I claim; how long can I draw unemployment benefit; insured earnings unemployment insurance; Wartetage; Wartezeit Arbeitslosenkasse; Anzahl Taggelder; versicherter Verdienst; Rahmenfrist fuer den Leistungsbezug; Bezugsdauer Arbeitslosenentschaedigung; besondere Wartetage; kontrollierter Arbeitslosigkeit; Taggelder; Rahmenfrist für den Leistungsbezug; Pauschalansatz; Beitragszeit befreit; Unterhaltspflicht; Krankentaggelder; Anspruchsvoraussetzungen
Questions: How many waiting days do I have to serve before I get my first unemployment payment?; Wie viele Wartetage muss ich bestehen, bevor das erste Taggeld ausbezahlt wird?
Published facts:
The first daily allowance is paid out only after the waiting days have been served, only days on which the person meets all the eligibility conditions count as waiting days, and entitlement generally begins after a general waiting period of 5 days of controlled unemployment.
The general waiting period is between 0 and 20 days and depends on the person's annual income and on whether they have a maintenance obligation, with no waiting days for the lowest income bracket, 5 days for the bracket above it without a maintenance obligation and 20 days for the highest income bracket without a maintenance obligation.
On top of the general waiting days, special waiting days must be served in certain cases - 1 day for a person who worked in a seasonal job or in an occupation with frequently changing or fixed-term employment, 5 days for a person exempt from the contribution period solely because of long illness, maternity, accident, invalidity, the death of a spouse, separation, divorce, a stay in a Swiss institution or a return from working abroad, and 120 days for a person exempt from the contribution period because of schooling, retraining or further training.
Unemployment insurance pays 5 daily allowances a week, from Monday to Friday, so the amount paid out each month varies with the number of working days in that month, and the level of the benefit depends on the wage subject to old-age insurance contributions that the person earned on average in the last 6 months or, if that is more favourable, in the last 12 months before unemployment, which is the insured earnings.
The unemployment benefit is 80 per cent of the insured earnings for a person who has maintenance obligations towards children under 25 years, for a person whose insured earnings do not exceed a franc limit the page states, or for a person who draws a disability pension corresponding to a degree of disability of at least 40 per cent, and it is 70 per cent of the insured earnings in all other cases.
Social insurance contributions are deducted from the unemployment benefit, and for foreign nationals who are liable to tax at source the withholding tax is deducted as well.
A person who is exempt from meeting the contribution period receives a daily allowance of 80 per cent of a lump-sum rate that depends on their education and age, and that rate is halved for a person who is exempt because of schooling, retraining, further training or the completion of an apprenticeship, is under 25 years old and has no maintenance obligations towards children.
Unemployment insurance provides for a maximum period of drawing benefit of 2 years, called the frame period for benefits, and that frame period starts on the first day on which the person meets all the eligibility conditions.
Certain categories of insured persons are entitled to an additional 120 daily allowances if they became unemployed within the last 4 years before reaching the reference age of the old-age insurance, and a person forced to take up or extend employment because a disability pension was reduced or discontinued is entitled to at most 180 daily allowances.
After an accident during unemployment the unemployment insurance pays benefits for the first 3 days including the day of the accident and the accident insurer pays daily allowances afterwards, whereas for an incapacity to work due to illness or pregnancy unemployment benefit is payable only for the first 30 calendar days of the incapacity and sickness daily allowances are limited to 44 daily allowances within the frame period for benefits.

Label: Taking a lower-paid job while unemployed
Description: Interim earnings are income from employed or self-employed work taken up during unemployment that is lower than the unemployment benefit. Instead of the entitlement stopping, the insurance pays a compensation payment on top, and the combination is always higher than the benefit alone. [SECO]
Aliases: interim earnings; Zwischenverdienst; compensation payment while unemployed; Kompensationszahlung; taking a lower-paid job while on unemployment benefit; working part-time while claiming unemployment benefit; schlechter bezahlte Stelle annehmen; orts- und betriebsüblich; Verlängerung der Bezugsdauer
Questions: If I take a job that pays less than my unemployment benefit, do I lose the benefit?; Was gilt als Zwischenverdienst und zahlt die Arbeitslosenversicherung etwas dazu?
Published facts:
Interim earnings are any income from employed or self-employed work earned during unemployment that is lower than the unemployment benefit, and in that case the unemployment insurance pays a compensation payment.
The compensation payment for interim earnings is paid for at least twelve months.
Interim earnings must be paid at the rate that is customary for the locality and for the industry.
Interim earnings and the compensation payment together are always higher than the unemployment benefit alone, interim earnings extend the period over which benefits can be drawn, and they build new contribution periods except where the interim earnings come from self-employed work.
Compensation payments for interim earnings are one of the benefits of the Swiss unemployment insurance alongside the unemployment benefit and the insolvency compensation, and all of these benefits are paid out by the responsible unemployment fund.

Label: Vacancies that must be reported to the RAV first
Description: Employers must report vacancies in occupation types with high unemployment to the responsible regional employment centre before advertising them publicly, on the basis of a list published every year. Jobseekers registered with an RAV therefore see those vacancies first. [SECO]
Aliases: job registration duty; Stellenmeldepflicht; vacancies reported to the RAV before public advertising; head start on job vacancies; Informationsvorsprung; meldepflichtige Berufsarten; Berufsarten mit hoher Arbeitslosigkeit; do registered jobseekers see jobs first; Liste der meldepflichtigen Berufsarten; Informations- und Bewerbungsvorsprung; Informationsvorsprung von fünf Arbeitstagen; meldepflichtig
Questions: Do jobseekers registered with the RAV really see some vacancies before the public?; Wie lange dauert der Informationsvorsprung bei der Stellenmeldepflicht?
Published facts:
In Switzerland the job-registration duty applies to occupation types with high unemployment.
The job-registration duty obliges employers, on the basis of the annually published list of occupation types subject to the duty, to report vacancies to the responsible regional employment centre before they are advertised publicly.
Because of the job-registration duty, jobseekers registered with an RAV in occupation types with high unemployment get an information and application head start over other candidates.
The job-registration duty has applied since 1 July 2018.
Employers can use the check offered by the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs to find out whether their vacancy is subject to the job-registration duty.
A vacancy subject to the job-registration duty can be reported directly on the Job-Room platform, or by telephone or in person at the responsible regional employment centre.
With a portal registration, which is open only to persons registered as jobseekers with a regional employment centre, a jobseeker has an information head start of five working days and can see at once the vacancies employers have reported under the job-registration duty.
The job-registration duty for occupation types with high unemployment was decided by parliament after the electorate accepted the initiative against mass immigration in February 2014, with the aim of making better use of the domestic workforce, and on 8 December 2017 the Federal Council set out how the constitutional article on steering immigration is implemented at ordinance level.

Label: Signing on with the RAV in the Canton of Zurich
Description: How a person in the Canton of Zurich signs on with their regional employment centre - when to register, online or in person, which unemployment fund to choose, and what the cantonal employment service asks of them around the registration interview. [Canton of Zurich]
Aliases: register as unemployed in Zurich; RAV registration Zurich; Anmeldung Arbeitslosenkasse; Arbeitslosenkasse waehlen; Anmeldegespraech RAV; zustaendiges RAV fuer Arbeitgeber; Regionalen Arbeitsvermittlungszentrum; Arbeitslosenkassen; E-Learning-Modul; Beratungsgespräche; Zugangsdaten; Stellensuchportal des Bundes; Postleitzahl Ihres Unternehmens
Questions: Can I register with the RAV online or do I have to go there in person?; Welche Arbeitslosenkasse kann ich im Kanton Zürich wählen?
Published facts:
In the Canton of Zurich a person who has been given notice or is unemployed must register with their responsible regional employment centre with the required documents already during the notice period and at the latest on the first day of unemployment, and unemployment insurance benefits can be drawn at the earliest from the date of that registration.
The Canton of Zurich offers two ways of signing on with the RAV - registering online or registering in person at the RAV - and registering early means a person can already use the RAV services during the notice period.
There are four unemployment funds in the Canton of Zurich, all of them providing the same services, and as part of registering with the RAV a person is asked to choose one of them.
The unemployment fund chosen at registration is the office that clarifies a person's entitlement to unemployment compensation, calculates the amount and the duration of their daily allowances and, where there is an entitlement, pays the daily allowances out monthly.
For jobseekers in the Canton of Zurich an e-learning module is available in several languages so that they know their rights and duties towards the unemployment insurance and are informed about the benefits and the deadlines.
The Canton of Zurich asks jobseekers not to bring small children to counselling interviews at the RAV, while another person may accompany them if translation is needed.
As soon as a person registers with the RAV they receive personal access credentials for the federal job portal, and with that login they can upload and manage their application documents and their own job-search efforts, which simplifies the exchange of data with their RAV counsellor.
An employer in the Canton of Zurich with a vacancy to fill finds the RAV responsible for them by entering the postal code of their company in the RAV finder, which is a separate search from the one jobseekers use for their place of residence.

Label: Short-time work compensation, seen from the employee
Description: Short-time work compensation covers part of the wage costs of employees whose hours are temporarily cut, so that a business can keep its staff instead of dismissing them. The business registers the short-time work in advance with the cantonal authority and accounts for it with an unemployment fund. [SECO]
Aliases: short-time work; short time work compensation; Kurzarbeit; Kurzarbeitsentschaedigung; reduced working hours; employer put us on short-time work; Arbeitsausfall; Kurzarbeitsentschädigung; Voranmeldefrist; kantonalen Amtsstelle; Karenzzeit; Höchstbezugsdauer; Arbeitszeitkontrolle; Voranmeldung; Mehrstunden; KAST
Questions: My employer has put us on short-time work - what does that mean for me?; Wer meldet die Kurzarbeit an und wie lange kann sie bezogen werden?
Published facts:
Short-time work compensation covers part of the wage costs of the employees affected by short-time work for a limited period, so that a business can keep qualified staff and avoid dismissals when short-term, unavoidable losses of work occur.
Short-time work can be applied for when the loss of work is temporary and does not belong to the normal operating risk, provided the legal requirements are met and the ordinary procedure is followed.
Short-time work has to be registered in advance with the competent cantonal authority, and a pre-notification period of normally 10 days applies; the page addresses this step to the business, whose wage costs the compensation covers, and not to the individual employee.
Short-time work is authorised each time for a period of up to 3 months.
The maximum period for drawing short-time work compensation is in principle 12 months within a two-year frame period; on 8 October 2025 the Federal Council decided to raise that maximum to 24 months, and the amended ordinance entered into force on 1 November 2025 and, after being extended on 27 May 2026, applies until 31 January 2027.
A waiting period of 1 working day a month applies to short-time work compensation, which the page calls the employer's own deductible.
Within one frame period at most 4 accounting periods with a loss of work of more than 85 per cent can be claimed.
Extra hours are deducted unless they are taken off as time before short-time work compensation is drawn.
For employees affected by short-time work the business must keep a working time control that shows, day by day, the hours actually worked including any extra hours, the economically caused lost hours and all other absences, and this condition also applies to people in management positions whatever their level.
Questions about the pre-notification of short-time work and about the entitlement are answered by the competent cantonal authority, while questions about the benefits and the accounting are handled by the chosen unemployment fund.

Label: Courses, employment programmes and allowances for jobseekers
Description: The labour-market measures are the courses, employment programmes, placements and allowances that support unemployed people and people threatened with unemployment back into work. The RAV assesses whether a measure is suitable and approves participation, so a jobseeker does not simply enrol. [SECO, Canton of Zurich]
Aliases: labour market measures; arbeitsmarktliche Massnahmen; course while unemployed; who pays for a course when unemployed; retraining while on unemployment benefit; Beschaeftigungsprogramm; Weiterbildung waehrend Arbeitslosigkeit; Kurs vom RAV bezahlt; Einarbeitungszuschuss; Umschulung Arbeitslosenversicherung; Zuweisung zu geeigneten Angeboten; Beteiligung an Kurskosten; Teilnahmekriterien für AMM; individuelles Kursgesuch; Beschäftigungsprogramme; Motivationssemester; Standortbestimmungs- und Bewerbungskurse; Wiedereingliederung
Questions: Can I do a course while I am unemployed, and who pays for it?; Wer entscheidet über die Teilnahme an einer arbeitsmarktlichen Massnahme?
Published facts:
The labour-market measures support unemployed people and people threatened with unemployment in returning quickly and lastingly to working life, with the aim of improving their employability and their chances of lasting employment, and the regional employment centre advises on them.
The measures are intended to help participants broaden their specialist knowledge, learn new techniques and methods, and build their professional network and new contacts.
The range of measures is broad and geared to different occupational situations, and an overview and description of all available offers is given in the list of measures.
Anyone who is entitled to unemployment benefit in principle also meets the conditions for taking part in labour-market measures.
People who are not yet entitled to unemployment benefit, for example because they are only threatened with unemployment, can also be supported under certain conditions, and in such cases a contribution towards course costs is possible.
Whether a measure is suitable and useful is in principle assessed by the regional employment centre, which takes into account the person's individual situation, their occupational background and their chances on the labour market.
The regional employment centre is responsible for advising on the measures, for checking whether the participation conditions are met, and for assigning jobseekers to suitable offers.
Taking part in a measure as a rule follows prior advice and examination by the regional employment centre, but insured persons may at any time submit an application to take part to their centre on their own initiative.
For courses and training placements the application must be submitted to the regional employment centre at least 10 days before the measure starts, and the centre provides the forms needed for registration and helps with filling them in if required.
Further information on the measures is available in the brochure of the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs, and questions can be put to a person's own regional employment centre.
In the Canton of Zurich the offer of the regional employment centres contains various courses and employment programmes, the labour-market measures, which support jobseekers in finding a job more quickly.
The measures offered in the Canton of Zurich are financed by the unemployment insurance and comprise a broad range of courses and programmes for the occupational reintegration of jobseekers, aiming to speed up a return to the labour market or to avoid impending unemployment.
A measure can be used in the Canton of Zurich where a jobseeker's employability is impaired for labour-market reasons, and jobseekers can either attend an offer from the collective courses and programmes, which are as a rule proposed by the responsible RAV adviser, or submit an individual course application.
The Canton of Zurich lists five conditions for taking part in a labour-market measure - the person is registered with the RAV, is unemployed or will soon be unemployed, the measure helps them find a job quickly, they meet the admission criteria of the providing institution, and their participation is approved by the RAV.
The kinds of measure listed by the Canton of Zurich include assessment and job-application courses, specialist courses, temporary employment programmes, motivation semesters, training and occupational placements, induction and training allowances, commuting-cost and weekly-residence contributions, and support for taking up self-employment.
For collective courses and programmes in the Canton of Zurich jobseekers should discuss suitable offers with their RAV adviser, and assessment and job-application courses are very often proposed shortly after registration with the RAV.
In the Canton of Zurich a jobseeker can apply for the financing of an individual further-training course, and the RAV can approve the application if the training considerably improves their chances in the job search; the jobseeker looks for suitable offers themselves, receives an application form from their RAV adviser and submits the completed form to their RAV.
The Canton of Zurich also points jobseekers to e-learning offers that help them find a job faster and improve their occupational qualifications, and says a selection of free offers is available.

Label: Running out of unemployment benefit
Description: What happens when the entitlement to unemployment benefit ends before the person has found work - what the regional employment centres still offer, when the entitlement can revive, and what changes for accident cover, old-age contributions, occupational pension cover and family allowances. [SECO]
Aliases: Aussteuerung; ausgesteuert; running out of unemployment benefit; unemployment benefit exhausted; keine Taggelder mehr; Ende des Taggeldanspruchs; what happens after unemployment benefits run out; Anspruch auf Arbeitslosenentschädigung; Regionalen Arbeitsvermittlungszentren; wieder aufleben; Abredeversicherung; nichterwerbstätig; Stiftung Auffangeinrichtung BVG; Familienzulagen
Questions: What happens when my unemployment benefit runs out?; Was passiert nach der Aussteuerung?
Published facts:
The end of the entitlement means that the entitlement to unemployment benefit ends before the person could return to the labour market, and those affected receive no further daily allowances.
Several forms of support remain available after the entitlement ends, from help with the job search and labour-market measures to what the municipality of residence offers.
The counselling and placement services of the regional employment centres remain available after the entitlement ends, that is once a person no longer receives daily allowances.
The page additionally recommends contacting private placement agencies directly and names the member list of the association of Swiss staffing service providers as a source of addresses of licensed agencies.
Under certain conditions labour-market measures can still be used after the entitlement ends, up to the end of the running frame period, and the personal RAV adviser gives further information about them.
In certain cases the entitlement to unemployment benefit can revive within the two-year frame period, and the person has to report the relevant circumstances to their last unemployment fund.
Unemployed people entitled to daily allowances are insured against accidents with the national accident insurance fund, and that cover ends 31 days after the entitlement to unemployment benefit ends.
Before those 31 days expire an agreement insurance can be taken out, which extends the accident cover against payment of a premium by up to six months, and if no agreement insurance is taken out or no new job is found within the extension the health insurer has to be notified.
After the entitlement ends the unemployment fund no longer settles the old-age insurance contributions, the person counts as non-employed and has to register with the compensation office of their canton of residence or with the responsible municipal branch, and missing contribution years can lead to a reduction of the later pension.
People who receive an unemployment insurance daily allowance above a threshold the page states are compulsorily insured against the risks of death and disability with the substitute occupational benefit institution, this cover continues for one further month after the entitlement ends, and if a new pension relationship starts in that time the new pension institution is responsible.
Once the daily allowance entitlement ends the unemployment insurance no longer pays the supplement for family allowances, and information on family allowances is given by the cantonal compensation offices and by the Federal Social Insurance Office.
For a financially difficult situation after the entitlement ends the page points people to the social assistance of their municipality of residence, with further information from that municipality or from the Swiss Conference for Social Welfare.
For personal counselling and further services the page tells people to contact their responsible regional employment centre or the responsible cantonal authority.

Label: When the employer goes bankrupt owing wages
Description: Insolvency compensation covers outstanding wage claims for work already done when the employer is unable to pay. It is paid to the employee by the unemployment fund, which then reclaims the money from the employer, and each employee applies individually within a deadline. [SECO, Canton of Zurich]
Aliases: insolvency compensation; Insolvenzentschaedigung; employer bankrupt unpaid wages; employer cannot pay my salary; offene Lohnforderungen; Arbeitgeber ist zahlungsunfaehig; Konkurs des Arbeitgebers Lohn; Insolvenzentschädigung; zahlungsunfähig; zuständige öffentliche Arbeitslosenkasse; Nachlassstundung; Konkursaufschub
Questions: My employer went bankrupt and still owes me wages - what can I claim?; Mein Arbeitgeber ist zahlungsunfähig und schuldet mir Lohn - was kann ich verlangen?
Published facts:
Insolvency compensation covers outstanding wage claims for work that has already been performed when the employer is unable to pay.
Insolvency compensation is paid for a maximum of four months and amounts to 100 per cent of the outstanding wage claim.
The insolvency compensation is paid out to the insured person, and the unemployment fund then reclaims the amount from the employer.
The application must be made individually by each employee, must be addressed to the responsible public unemployment fund, and is subject to deadlines that have to be met.
Insolvency compensation is one of the benefits of the Swiss unemployment insurance, which supports people affected by unemployment or by the insolvency of their employer.
In the Canton of Zurich the application for insolvency compensation must be submitted at the latest 60 days after the publication of the bankruptcy, of the composition moratorium or of a judicial deferral of bankruptcy in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce, after the execution of the attachment, or after becoming aware that the deadline for the advance of costs expired unused following a bankruptcy petition, and it goes to the public unemployment fund of the canton in which the employer had its seat.
If that 60-day deadline is not met, any entitlement to insolvency compensation lapses, and the deadline cannot be extended.
The Canton of Zurich states that the outstanding wages must have been demanded from the employer at the latest after about 3 months for a person to be entitled to apply for insolvency compensation.
A person working for an insolvent employer in Switzerland is entitled to insolvency compensation if bankruptcy is opened over the employer, if bankruptcy is not opened only because no creditor will advance the costs given the employer's obvious over-indebtedness, if the person has filed an attachment request against the employer for wage claims, if a composition moratorium has been granted, or if there is a judicial deferral of bankruptcy.
There is no entitlement to insolvency compensation for persons who, as partners, as financially involved in the business or as members of a top decision-making body, determine or significantly influence the employer's decisions, and the same applies to co-working spouses of the employer and to persons who have already passed the ordinary retirement age of the old-age insurance.
The wage components are covered by insolvency compensation for at most the four months before the last day actually worked, and the insured earnings are capped at a monthly ceiling the page states.
In principle only contractually agreed wage components that are subject to old-age insurance contributions are insured, such as the wage, the thirteenth monthly wage, the holiday share, gratuities and compensated advance working time.
Responsible for paying out insolvency compensation are the public unemployment funds of the canton in which the affected company has its registered office, and if that office is in the Canton of Zurich it is the unemployment fund of the Canton of Zurich, which also supports employers facing bankruptcy with information events for the employees concerned.
For legal reasons the Zurich unemployment fund requires the signed documents of an insolvency compensation application to be submitted by post and cannot accept them by e-mail.
Outstanding child allowances for the period before the opening of bankruptcy must be claimed directly from the family compensation fund of the former employer, and if that fund is not known the person should contact the social insurance institution of the Canton of Zurich.
If none of the five qualifying events applies, the person should demand the outstanding wages from the employer by registered letter and, if the employer does not pay within a reasonable period, may start debt enforcement proceedings through a debt collection office.
A person who also wants to claim unemployment benefits alongside insolvency compensation must register with the regional employment centre at the latest after the last day actually worked for the insolvent employer, and at the Zurich unemployment fund both benefits are handled by the same department.

Label: Unemployment insurance across the EU and EFTA border
Description: What happens to unemployment insurance when work or a job search crosses the border between Switzerland and an EU or EFTA state - the condition attached to a Swiss claim after working abroad, the portable document U1 that certifies insurance periods completed elsewhere, the portable document U2 that allows benefit to be drawn while looking for work in another state, and the EURES network. [SECO]
Aliases: PD U1; PD U2; portable document U1; portable document U2; EURES; export of unemployment benefit; Leistungsexport; Arbeitslosengeld im Ausland beziehen; Beitragszeiten im Ausland; im EU-Ausland gearbeitet und jetzt arbeitslos; returning to Switzerland after working abroad; Stellensuche im EU-Ausland; EURES-Portal; beruflichen Mobilität; Beitragszeit; tragbare Dokumente; Versicherungszeiten; EU/EFTA-Staat
Questions: I worked in Germany for three years and am moving back to Switzerland - can I claim Swiss unemployment benefit?; Wer stellt das Formular PD U1 aus und wofür brauche ich es?
Published facts:
EURES is a cooperation network of the public employment administrations of the European Union and of the member states of the European Free Trade Association, and with more than 1,000 EURES advisers and the central EURES portal it supports jobseekers and employers with professional mobility, the portal giving access to job vacancies and to information on living and working in the EU and EFTA.
EURES Switzerland does not itself place people in jobs, but the EURES portal lists the vacancies published in the EU and EFTA member states, and EURES advisers in every member state give information on the European labour market and on professional mobility and help with the application dossier in the target country.
A person who lives in a member state of the EU or EFTA and has worked there may register with a regional employment centre in Switzerland, but a claim to benefits of the Swiss unemployment insurance exists only if that person has sufficient contribution time in Switzerland.
A person who does not have sufficient contribution time for the Swiss unemployment insurance must, before returning to Switzerland, apply for an export of benefits with the form PD U2 at the competent authority of their place of residence in the EU or EFTA state, and the country they return from then pays them the unemployment benefit for a limited duration of at most 3 to 6 months.
The portable document PD U2 is the authorisation to draw unemployment benefit while looking for work in another EU or EFTA state, and for a person returning to Switzerland it is issued by the public employment service or the competent social insurance institution of the state they are returning from.
The portable document PD U1 certifies insurance periods for the calculation of unemployment benefits and is issued by the public employment service or the competent social insurance institution of the EU or EFTA state or states in which the person was employed.
A person registered as unemployed in Switzerland may look for work in an EU or EFTA state and continue to draw unemployment benefit, an export of benefits that is possible only to an EU or EFTA state, is limited to at most three months and must be applied for at the competent regional employment centre before departure, which issues the form PD U2 if the conditions are met.
In Switzerland the portable document PD U1 is issued by an unemployment fund, which needs the application form and information on whether the person was already registered with a fund or has drawn benefits, and a person not previously registered sends the documents to a fund of their choice at their last place of residence in Switzerland, or at the registered office of their last employer if they did not live in Switzerland.

Label: Notice periods, protection against dismissal, and the work reference
Description: What the SECO page on the first steps after notice states of the Code of Obligations rules that apply when no notice period is agreed in writing and no collective agreement applies. It carries the four statutory notice periods, the three periods during which no notice may be given, and the right to a work reference. It is a short extract and not a treatment of Swiss employment law. [SECO, OR]
Aliases: notice period; statutory notice period; how much notice must my employer give; protection against dismissal; dismissal during illness; dismissal during pregnancy; work reference; confirmation of employment; Kuendigungsfrist; gesetzliche Kuendigungsfrist; Kuendigungsfrist Probezeit; Kuendigungsschutz; Kuendigung waehrend Schwangerschaft; Arbeitszeugnis verlangen; Arbeitsbestaetigung; Kündigungsfrist; Obligationenrecht; Gesamtarbeitsvertrag; Probezeit; Dienstjahr; Kündigungsschutz; Schutzdienst; Niederkunft; Arbeitszeugnis; Arbeitsbestätigung; eingeschriebenem Brief; wohlwollend und wahrheitsgetreu
Questions: How long is the notice period if my employment contract says nothing about it?; Wie lang ist die Kündigungsfrist im dritten Dienstjahr?
Published facts:
The employer must observe the notice period, and where no notice period is agreed in writing and no collective labour agreement applies, the rules of the Swiss Code of Obligations apply.
Under those rules the notice period during the probation period is 7 days, and notice may take effect at the end of any day.
Under those rules the notice period in the first year of service is 1 month, and notice may take effect at the end of a month.
Under those rules the notice period from the 2nd to the 9th year of service is 2 months, and notice may take effect at the end of a month.
Under those rules the notice period from the 10th year of service onwards is 3 months, and notice may take effect at the end of a month.
A special protection against dismissal applies during military service, civilian service or civil-protection service, in the event of illness or accident, and during pregnancy and the 16 weeks after the birth.
No notice of termination may be given while the protection against dismissal applies.
Anyone unsure whether the protection against dismissal applies to them should tell the employer immediately by registered letter that they want to continue working.
An employee should request from the employer a work reference, or at least a confirmation of employment covering the duration of the employment, because a complete dossier is needed to apply for a new job.
The employer is obliged to write the work reference benevolently and truthfully.
